review:
9/1 開始　47h プレイした感想

全体的に荒削りでバグもかなり多いがアプデ頻度はこの数日間でも2.3回？入っていたので運営のやる気は感じられます。(序盤にやる気を出しすぎてどんどん更新頻度が落ちていったDungeon Bornのようにならないことを祈ります)
個人的に一番やばいなと思ったバグはタスクの進捗状況がリセットされるものでした。
ロビーのスタッシュ画面にてバックパックを掴んだまま何故か離せないバグが発生し整理ができなくなった為、アプリを再起動した結果
タスクが全て初期化
掴まれたままのバックパックは消失
郵便受けの中身も消失
設計図も使用して解禁されたもの全て消えていました。
キャラクターデータ、倉庫のアイテム、ハイドアウト等は残ったままでした。
その後何事も無かったかのようにタスクを進めてそろそろ全てのタスクが終わりそうな雰囲気を醸し出している気もします。今のところタスク初期化バグにもう一度あたるといった悲劇には見舞われていません。

不満点を挙げるとすれば、
・ボスクラス？の敵は攻撃に吹き飛ばし属性がデフォルトになっており狭い場所で食らったらそのまま
吹き飛ばし(受け身不可)→起き上がるまでにもっかい吹き飛ばされるの繰り返しでもっていかれたりします。
起き上がりの際にローリング起き上がりみたいなのあってもいいのではないかなと思ったり思わなかったり。
今のところトロールだかオーガだかにはめ殺されたのが1回のみなので神経質になるほどでもないのかなとも思います。
・魔法に対して弓があまりにも貧弱です。
魔法はほぼノーリソースでドカドカ撃てるXのに対して弓は矢と言うリソースを支払って攻撃しているにもかかわらず爪楊枝でも撃ち込んでいるのか思うくらい弱く再序盤で使用するのをやめました。(矢尻をいいものして使えば使えるのかは検証していません。)
※魔法は連発しすぎると汚染ゲージが溜まって体が爆散して即死して死体も残らないのでマルチでもアイテム回収できないので注意してください。
・刺突属性の武器があまりにも弱く現状使用する価値がないのでうまい具合にテコ入れしてもいいと思います。
・ある程度プレイしているとお金の使い道が無くて困ってくるのでお金の使い道が欲しい
・タスクアイテムを入手しそのアイテムを納品すると入手の条件が満たされていないことになり結果的に同じタスクアイテムが二個必要になり二度手間なのでめんどくさい(直せないならタスク条件から入手を消してほしい)
・クラフトアイテムが最初から全て開示されている
個人的にハイドアウトの進捗に合わせてレシピは解放していく方針の方が楽しいのではないかなと
・ほんのわずかな段差を乗り越えられない
(ジャンプとかしゃがみ動作や乗り越えを実装してほしい)

プレイしてて感じたのはこれくらいです。
最適化とかバグの部分に関してはデモ版なのであれこれ言うほどの事でもないかなと
少なくとも自分は3~4日間でこれだけ遊んでるくらいには楽しめてます。

PC specs are absurd, asking for 8 GB VRAM (when RDR2 only asks for 2 GB) is extremely amateurish and clearly a crutch for lackluster optimization. This is unacceptable for an indie game, its a very clear example of "Unreal slop".

Possible optimization improvements: 
[list]
    [*]LOD's (not just Nanite, actual LOD's)
    [*]Occlusion culling
    [*]Object pooling (if it applies)
    [*]Resolution scaling
    [*]Avoid the use of volumetrics (since they are very performance costly and have much better alternatives)
    [*]Avoid the use of Nanite and learn how to properly make lowpoly 3D assets with baked maps.
    [*]Bake texture atlasses on compilation time to reduce texture draw calls in runtime
    [*]Bake static lighting and avoid excessive usage of runtime lighting calculation
[/list]

thoughts:

Its not terrible? In its current state its a definite no though.

Pros:

game has decent enough graphics
the sound quality is nice
i like the variety of items you can loot
the spooky ambiance is definitely there

Cons: 

you walk and swing your weapon like a drunk person would.

the game is unreasonably dark. I'm talking switch to a bow and suddenly you're blind. Why even have options to use other equips, if a torch is mandatory for 95% of a run? 

the inventory system desperately needs a rotate item option. Often you will find equips you cant take. You have the space, but its impossible because you cant rotate the items in your inventory to be vertical or horizontal. 

Sometimes the game throws an unreasonable amount of enemies at you. running is not always an option. So just die i guess?

Death makes you lose whatever you brought with you, okay that's fine, but what to do when you lose all your weapons from dying? Just pray to god you find a weapon before you die i guess? *shrug*

There is a lot of stuttering and lag, this needs to be ironed out, it happens most often in combat or near fires. I can run fully modded skyrim with shadders bro, there's no reason this game lags besides poor optimization

As is, its not a bad game, but it needs a lot a lot of work still.

Overall: 6.5/10

It feels like a bunch of amateur devs who love dark and darker started learning ue5 together and took on a project with much larger scope than they could handle. It was a fun janky mess for an hour or so with friends, but this game needs so so much work. I wouldn't bet on it having a redemption arc in the future unless they can pull off a miracle.

There's passion behind it in some areas. You can clearly see the inspiration for some of the mechanics and such, but if you're looking at it overall, it's just not good enough.

The performance and optimization is completely awful. The ui is unintuitive. Actually, pretty much everything about the game is unintuitive. Some of the good features feel forgotten, and some of the bad features feel too elevated. Again, there's potential here, but I really doubt them being able to pull this together into a cohesive, fun game. (But it's worth giving it a try, don't just read reviews. It's a free demo, try it out yourself and make your own opinion.)

¿Te gustan las mazmorras? ¿Te gusta la estrategia? ¿Te gusta pasarla bien con amigos? ¿Te gustan los desafíos? ¿Te gusta lotear? ¿Te gusta gestionar tu propio campamento, vender objetos, completar misiones? ¿Te gusta echarte un buen rato con tus compas? ¿Te gusta pelear contra jefes y criaturas realmente difíciles?

Déjame decirte que este juego es para ti. Es de entender que es una demo, pero por dios, que buenos gráficos, iluminación y ambientación. Es realmente bueno, se ha convertido en uno de mis juegos favoritos de mazmorras.

Sí, la creación del personaje es algo escaza, algunos movimientos se sienten algo toscos, pero TODO LO OTRO lo compensa, y no solo eso, tiene un potencial tremendo, tiene TODO para convertirse en un juegazo. Lo recomiendo al 100%, es una gran experiencia.

４時間ほどプレイ、まず一言で言うとバカおもろい。

ただかなり重めのグラとバグが多めなのが難点かな。自分のpcの仕様で、最低画質（ほぼ画質変わってない）にしてもたまーにカクつく。バグも割と深刻なバグがあって戦闘中に武器が使えなくなることもある。まぁまだ発売前なのでしょうがないといえばしょうがない。
内容を簡単に言えば、dadやtarkovのように金品稼いで脱出するっていう感じ。
ただ他とは違うのは何よりPVE限定なこと。
気軽に遊べて対人ゲーのようなストレスもない。なので前述したゲームと比べてだいぶ簡単。
油断すると普通に死にかけるけどね。
あとかなり稼ぎやすい。ここらへんは好みが分かれるかもしれない。
それから魔法を使えるようになってから面白さが倍増する。dadと違い詠唱を必要とし、４つの種類のなんか属性みたいなのを矢印キー（初期設定）で選択して並べていく感じ。その組み合わせで魔法が発動できる。
ただ、代償として体が蝕まれる。これは時間経過ですぐ治っていく感じ。まぁ魔法版スタミナだと思うとわかりやすいかも。

I don't review games often, but this one scratches an itch I didn't know I even had.

I'm going to lead with the negative, because I don't want to be misleading, if you are looking for a fully fledged experience this isn't it yet.

Not going to sugar coat it, its in a very early state and it has all the hallmarks of that. There are bugs, things are poorly balanced or outright missing, the maps and enemy variety are sparse.

THAT BEING SAID

The atmosphere is top notch, and the maps that we do have are excellent. The sound effects, and danger (Especially early on) are palpable, you will be lost, out of supplies and be fighting for your life to get a cool backpack or hand tool you found out.

Your friends will get surrounded, and you will do everything in your power to save them, and it creates great gameplay moments, when a boss enemy comes through a wall after you.

You will make a cool new sword or find a new spell, and then blow yourself up or lose it.

This game has a ton of potential, and I can't wait for them to come out with more.

+ 분위기가 압도적이다. : 

다 무너진 중세배경의 마을과 성은, '도대체 내가 앞으로 뭘 상대해야 하는가' 싶은 불안감으로 사람을 위축되게 만든다. 

지상은 안개가 빽빽하여 인게임 캐릭터 기준으로 스무걸음 앞이 잘 안보이는 수준이며, 

지하는 새까만 어둠이 벽 뒤, 방 구석, 문 너머를 미지 그 자체로 만들어 걸음을 내딛는 것을 주저하게 한다.

공통적으로 지상이나 지하 둘다 들려오는 몬스터들의 괴상한 울음이나, 낄낄거리는 웃음소리는, 

안그래도 정찰병 역할의 몬스터가 존재해, '가능한 한 들키면 안되며, 큰 전투는 피해야한다.' 는 압박감에 더해,

내가 어딧는지도 제대로 파악을 못한 몹을 피해가야할지 맞서야할지 고민하게 만들고, 신경을 곤두세운다.


+ 파밍이라는 보상체계가 인게임 콘텐츠 상으로 밸런싱이 아주 잘 잡혀있다. 그리고 그게 너무 재밋다. :

아이탬이 다양하고, 도구, 잡탬, 염료, 장비, 도면 등등 각 분류마다 비싸거나 많이 필요한 것들이 두서가지씩은 꼭있다.

어지간한 물건들이 전부 던전 안에서 꽤 희소하게 드롭되는데다가,

심지어는 내 기지를 꾸려갈때 필수적인 물자들이 전부 드롭확률이 낮은 축에 속하며, 그 제작도면은 더욱 안나온다.

그렇기에 분명 PVE여서 게임의 난이도가 꽤 낮음에도 불구하고 여러번 반복해서 끊임없이 들어가야하고, 

아이템 테이블 (맵에서 등장 할 수 있는 아이템목록)이 지상과 지하 서로 틀리니, 그 횟수는 두배로 늘어난다.

횟수가 늘어나는만큼, 게임의 난이도가 어렵진 않지만 반복이 되니 억까를 당할 확률도 올라가고,

사고를 당하면 가방을 포함한 모든 아이템을 잃게 되어 친구가 주워주지않으면 회수할 방법이 없고,

마력폭발로 죽어버리는 사고는 시체마저 남지 않아 회수 자체가 불가능하니,

좋은 장비를 입을 수록 오히려 죽을까봐 불안감은 증폭된다.

좋은 보상이 나오는 곳은 서로 꽤 멀리 떨어져있는지라 이동거리가 꽤 되는데,

한 곳만 털고 나오자니 아쉽고, 더 털자니 사고가 날 것 같아 두려워지게 만든다.

아 물론, 이 맛있는 긴장감은, 데모를 하면서 '아 여기에서 나를 해할수 있는건 오우거 뿐이군.' 라는 깨달음과 함께 사라져버렸다.

- 몬스터의 레벨 밸런싱이 너무 안잡혀있다. :

스켈레톤은 qudtls이다. 느리고, 그나마 몹같은 언데드 마법사는 쉴드만 터트리면 죽어버린다.

숫자로 밀어붙히자는 콘셉같은데, 느릿느릿하고 잘 죽지않는 대신, 죽여도 죽여도 끝이 없이 느껴지려면,

데모기준보다 한 3배는 되어야할 것이다. 지상같은 경우, 스켈레톤이 나오는 순간 그냥 프리파밍이다.

석궁 사수와 롱보우 사수 스켈레톤은 아군 오사하기에 바쁘고, 언데드 메이지는 잘 안보이는데다,

장창병은 쉴드 하나만 들고있어도 대처가능하고, 나머진 그냥 바보등신이다.

그나마 약간 몹다운 면이라면 가끔 10번 죽여도 다시 일어나는 무한 부활 특성 정도일까?

근데 이것도 은으로 떡칠한 장검 하나만 있으면 스켈레톤을 전부 개 간식으로 만들 수 있으니 하등 의미없다 하겠다.

부패한 기사를 포함한 모든 스켈레톤 몹의 숫자를 약 3배 가량 늘려버리던가, 혹은 다른 몹이 필요하다.

육신족은 분위기만 잡는 광대다. 소리랑 모션만 무섭다. 안그래도 텍스쳐가 뭉개져있어서 무섭지 않은데,

가까이 왔을때 몸을 날려와 맞아보면 데미지도 시원찮고, 모션들이 일률적인데다 내구성도 약하니,

검으로 세로베기를 해 쪼개버리면 검이 닿을 때마다 깍두기가 되어버려 김이 샌다.

황소마저, 대방패 하나만 있으면 모든 공격을 원천봉쇄하고, 그나마 잡기공격이 통하는데,

잡기공격 또한 보통 탱커가 맞는데다가, 그 탱커는 높은 수준의 방어구로 둘둘 싸매져 있을게 뻔하지 않은가.

고블린이 그나마 가장 말이 되는 밸런싱을 갖고 있었다.

특히 오우거야말로 엄청난 공포였는데, 이 오우거는 잡기 공격을 했을 시 일정확률로 즉사공격을 건다.

사람을 잡아 어금니로 머리를 씹고 뜯어내버리는데, 시전해서 씹힘을 당하는 즉시 시체가 된다.

이 부분은 약간 어이가 없었는데, 오우거가 이 처형모션이 실행되고 나면, 그 많은 오우거 피통을 깎기 전까진,

머리통이 씹힐 운명에 처한 내 불쌍한 동료를 구할 방법 자체가 존재하지 않는다.

고블린들은 이동속도도 빠르고, 숫자도 많으며, 원거리 사수들 또한 두마리씩은 꼭 데려오고,

갑옷을 입고 다니거나 방패를 들기 때문에, 어느 방향으로 검의 궤적을 잡든, 그 갑옷이나 방패가 보통 한번은 막아준다.

고블린 검이나 단검, 혹은 미늘창에 맞으면, 

전방에서 들어오는 공격은 낮은 확률로, 후방에서 들어오는 공격은 꽤 높은 확률로 '열상'이라는 상태이상에 걸리는데,

붕대를 감기 전까진 치유되지 않으며, 그 어떤 상태이상보다도 많은 데미지를 자랑한다.

적군 종족이 셋인데 하나는 맞아죽으면 그 맞아죽은 놈이 qudtls인 똥멍청이 몹이고,

또 하나는 분위기만 잡는데에 더해, 떼거리로 나오거나, 혹은 특수몹이 다수 등장하지 않는 이상 '써는 맛이 일품인 고깃덩이' 몹이고,

마지막 하나는 잘못 걸렸다 싶으면 도망가는 것 외에는 방법이 없으니 이건 밸런싱을 과연 하긴 한건가 싶다.

적으로 나오는 세 종족 다, 더 많은 기획과 그 반영이 필요하다.

- 마법 만능 게임. 이럴거면 석궁과 활, 총은 왜 만들어놨는가.

이 게임에서 속성 공격은 거의 만능이다.

위에서 설명했듯, 마법을 지나치게 남발하여, 자신이 마력중독으로 터져죽는 거대한 페널티를 제외하면,

불 마법은 적들이 순간 비명을 지르고 날뛰게하여 잠시동안 움직임을 무력화 할 수 있고, 범위도 넓다.

전기 마법은 잠시 몹들이 마비가 되는데, 미완성인지, 몇몇은 안통한다.

얼음 마법은 몹들이 얼어붙는데, 사람 근처에 뛰어와서 둘러싸놓곤 얼어붙어, 검도 시연용 허수아비로 변모한다.

마력탄은 건물들을 깨부술수 있기 때문에, 잠겨있는 문도 그냥 마력탄으로 몇번 매너없이 강력하게 노크하면,

벽 째로 부숴지면서, 내 허리 춤의 열쇠고리와 그 안에 담겨있는 여러개의 열쇠를 보며 '도대체 넌 왜 존재하는걸까?' 하는 의문을 품게 만든다.

와중, 본인은 석궁, 활, 총을 써보고 굉장히 놀랐는데, 진심으로 말한다만 왜 존재하는지 모르겠다.

일반몹 조차 머리에 대고 쏴도 죽지않는다. 왜 존재하는지 의문이다. 

장전이 빠른것도 아니고, 대형몹의 잡기 모션을 캔슬 할 수 있는 것도 아니다.

This is only a demo, but it's the most engaging demo I have ever been hooked on.
I will list the pros and cons but bare in mind that some if not many things are either not working, buggy, or implemented.

Pros:
- The action, there's just something very satisfying when you slay an enemy, a goblin gets slashed down, a fleshkin zombie exploding, a skeleton crumbling to pieces. The combat is "simple" but there are complexities to it with having to manage your stamina, your attack direction, being mindful of your surrounding so your weapon doesn't bounce off the environment, and no spamming attacks because it queues up all your inputs.
- For a game with low spec requirements it looks really dang good. probably in part with the lighting and the darkness masking any imperfections in the graphics.
- Customization is fun, from making the clothing to the color you want, to making your own personal weapon that you can name with parts to make your weapon more deadly. For a demo there are many things you can do to customize your weapon and it's good.
- 5 player coop pve, that's pretty great and lots of fun when we're all trying to survive, loot, and escape alive.
- There is so much to loot. if you're a loot gremlin this game is for you. Many many items to loot on the map to make yourself stronger, build up your base, things for quest lines, etc.
- 50 quests, for a demo it sure gives you a lot to do.
- PvE focused over PvP, there will be pvp but it's more of an afterthrough. the PvE is where the main focus is.
- The music and sound work is good. it sounds great, very fitting of the mood.

Cons:
- Skills not implemented, most of them are not working or working as intended which messed up my build but it's not a huge deal. Some skills could use a buff to make them better than what it is currently.
- the drop rates of items you NEED: This part is a natural part of any game with loot. however some of the vital material you need for quests or your base upgrade has a lot of randomness before you even get what you're looking for.
- UI, the user interface could be a tad more refined, because first time I played the game some of the options or different pages weren't obvious to me until someone pointed out I could flip through pages within the menu. Not the tabs on top, but the tab category. Ex. I didn't realize in the CAMP section you could flip to different parts of it to upgrade and thought, wow I only got a tent.

I could list more cons but it's one of those, it's a demo and it's only a matter of time before they fix or add things to the game.

I can't wait for the full release of the game with all the looting and slaying we'll be doing.
For a demo I cant believe the features I cant believe the customization. I cant believe the combat styles this a up and comer for sure. Hopefully they stick with it.

Disclaimer: The game is in essentially an alpha/early beta state right now (Aug 2026), if you don't like dealing with some jank then simply wait till more patches drop. The game shows great potential and is great fun even in it's incomplete state.

The good: 
-The game simply fun, the looting and extraction based gameplay is engaging and great to enjoy with friends
-A great aesthetic, with a wide variety of weapons and armor (some still being made)
-Combat is simple, yet still offers a variety of ways to engage enemies.  Even at ~150 hours in I am testing new weapon setups.
-Map design is great, exploring and doing quests offers ~30 hours of fresh gameplay (with more coming)
-LOOT! If you are a fellow Loot Goblin and enjoy having large pile of 500 different items you may never use then this game is for you!

The Bad:
- As of writing this review the game is a bit buggy, has sub-par optimization (patch for this in the works), and several major parts of the game are simply not finished yet (magic, wood types, and the skill tree are missing/largely incomplete).  All things that will be fixed by full release, do not mistake this for a complete game in it's current state (Aug 2026)
- The game needs some balancing, some common drops players need for basic crafting are incredibly rare *coughHandPlanecough*, and the game fails to offer enough threat to highly geared players to match the same intense gameplay loop that makes the first ~30 hours in this game so much fun. (again, all easily addressable in time)
-Graphics and enemy variety are on the lower end.  With a small team (~10 devs) this is to be expected, and several new enemy types have already been leaked by the devs.  Just don't expect the enemy quality and variety of a FromSoft game.
-Inventory.  If you HATE inventory management then you might need to steer clear of this game.  The looting/extraction loop frequently has you overburdened with valuable items trying to desperately find and extract, only to extract and have to sort out a bunch of inventory space to save things in your limited stash space.  While this creates a great feeling of surviving from moment to moment, mission to mission, with whatever you have on hand, it definitely has some tedium attached with it.  While I feel the system is implemented well, this will be a deal breaker for some players for sure.
Great game, very fun cant complain
So much potential for this. Will be watching closely.

To start, this is a review of the Demo after just 4 hours. I plan to revise this review after more time played (which there is definitely more time to be played) and after the full game comes out.

TL:DR - game needs a bit of polish, and one or two more mechanics wouldn't go amiss. Overall I really enjoy the game for it's immersion into dungeon diving, both the actual game play and the preparation work that can go a long way in how smooth the run goes. If you love the idea of going deep into a dungeon to bring back the finest items, you'll probably love this game play!

Let's start with the bad in my eyes. 

-When you die, everything on your is gone. In a PvPvE game I could totally understand this. Your body is gonna be taken apart by other players quickly, Even if you could somehow get back into the same lobby, I wouldn't expect to find my stuff un-pilfered. However in a PvE only game, I would love to see a feature allowing me to dive back in, collect my body, and hoist it out of the dungeon for a return of the gear found on it. I don't want to loot it like a corpse per-se (I don't want nude runs to recover gear) but a full body recovery system where you go in and carry it out sounds great to me in this atmosphere.

-The game lacks some level of explanation of UI systems. I think the UI in camp could do with some polishing. In particular, the crafting of weapons is great, but can be confusing. If you don't have 15 mins to just tinker around with it before you dive back into the dungeon it could be very frustrating. I know the internet has solved such issues in games long ago with forums and the like. However I don't think that is an excuse for the devs to forgo explanations of basic mechanics like adjusting your weapons and armor to better fit the enemies you are expecting to face. Like swapping out my halberds spike for a hammer when I know Skeletons are on the horizon. That said, I quite like the air of mystery and figuring out how the dungeon itself works when out on an expedition.

Those are really the only things I've been miffed by so far. I have been far more impressed with the game than disappointed, and here are some of the main reasons why. Let me be clear, I know not all people will like these systems and in some cases may even call them friction mechanics. Frankly I find them immersing and fun.

- Limited carry capacity. When you first dive into the dungeon, even with both a bag and a backpack, you will find your inventory filling up fast. Long before your actual carry capacity gets reached. Bulky items like Armor and weapons take up a LOT of space. The reason I like this is because it encourages learned the map, and deciding where you are going to loot before you ever even enter the dungeon. You don't want to fill your bags with every little thing you come across so you can sell it for a few pennies when you return. On my favorite runs, you often will delve into the dungeon for five to ten minutes to get some where, fighting a party or two of monsters on the way, before you even pick up a single piece of loot. Then once your bags are filled with the good stuff, you mosey on back out the way to you came, which leads me to my next favorite thing so far.

-No Map. I'm sure maps will pop up online before long (a quick google just showed me there are at least 2 out there already, though one appears to have been deleted?) but to me, exploring a new place like this is so much fun! As well has needing to remember where you came from to get back out. Retreating in a panic is a great way to get yourself killed. You need to be calm and collected as your retrace your steps to return to safety with your bag of goodies.

-Weapon crafting. In particular, the fact that it's not just using the same raw ingredients in ever larger quantities to get a better version of the exact same weapon. I'm talking about taking the haft of a weapon, and swapping out pommels, cross guards, blade/striker head types/ grips. It is a ton of fun collecting a few parts and then customizing your weapon based on what the game warns you is waiting in the dungeon that run. Skeletons? bring something to pulverize those bones! Fleshkin? make sure you have a sharp blade! Goblins who make sure of armor but are soft on the inside? puncturing weapons will hit the spot! You can use the same weapon haft (determining the move set) and alter the actual striking portion of the weapon to meet your needs!

-Consumable weapons are powerful! I can't count the number of games that make things like grenades and other throwables feel so... optional. In Expedition throwables can completely change a fight around. solo against eight enemies can be daunting, result in several potions being used, and taking a lot of time. A single explosive pot or fire vial can completely wipe those eight enemies out. Of course they can also be expensive... But it is a well worth trade off for how much effect they can be!

This game is a lot of fun, and has a lot of potential once you figure out the menu. I think a small tutorial of the main screen would help immensely. Once they can work out performance issues and some bugs it'll be a good co-op experience. I was killed by a chest at one point because it launched me into the sky for some reason. I would like to see more difficulty scaling for co-op, or a difficulty slider of some sort. As of now there isn't one and if one is added I hope they go the route of significantly increasing enemy spawn as opposed to. The trailer of the game makes it seems like like a left 4 dead style hoard but the enemy density was underwhelming based on the trailer. All in all, I am very excited for this game

Couple things to note here is that I've been into this game since second Playtest and have spent a good bit of time considering this game. I'm very excited for it and to see what will become of this game as the devs put more work into it. The other is that I haven't been able to really test and fiddle with all game aspects as I wanted to really give a proper review so this will simply be observations.

More work is definitely required on a few aspects of the game, primarily in giving clear definition as to what armament components and skills do. For melee weapons, they've got a good system and tool tip information as to what the components add to the weapon are spot on; but for a modular arrow/bolt system there are numerous head and fletching types that don't tell you much of anything as to what they mechanically do. Flavor and style is nice but I prefer to know what kind of actual function I'm getting. Especially when it comes to skills.

Combat I like, but the requirement to waste a skill perk on the ability to actively control the direction of your swings should be reconsidered. I get the 'training' aspect for the skills, I do, but that's what a lot of people are likely trashing on the combat aspect for. It's hoard combat vs solo/small squad so swing control is important especially dealing with corners and doorways, As it stands now, with the right weapon configuration handling monsters with melee if they're not the Large enemies is great. 

Ranged combat is in need of more attention, primarily in defining the utility of the arrow head types and letting players see what the munitions will do for their gameplay. There's, once again, a perk to put an aiming reticle, while reflecting 'training' not a fan.

Magic is interesting in how its done, I've had fun with the gameplay in solo but from reading the woes of others and being accidentally killed by teammates because a firebolt went towards them instead of an enemy has me figuring that the magic system needs further development.

Gear/clothing is half-way decent, it's part of the primary loot cycle, finding good gear in the dungeon isn't too difficult if you look in the correct spots and go for specific material types. I personally skipped all copper/bronze items and sought out iron or better, haven't had a bad time since, especially with their new system of adding resistences against elemental components to the gameplay. Very neat, but a defining feature to them as well as weapons is durability and there's no clear explaination as to repairs or maintenence of anything despite pretty much everything having a durability meter. This is detractive even despite how long gear tends to last, once durability starts hitting a certain threshold the stats begin decreasing accordingly with no clear way to bring them back up despite repair kits existing. There's also no field repair options, so you can't patch up a damaged weapon or armor to get you through a run that I've been able to see. 

Weight AND space managment is tedious, especially with how much space certain supplies need and how much weight they contribute per piece in a stack. BIGGEST is Building supplies. Very low stack count to weight ratio and they take up a major chunk of space in a very limited inventory; while there's 'ways' (see skills) to increase your carry capacity it's only by 10 units. and more skills reduce the weight of clothing and armor worn by small percentagaes and those are NOT quickly reachable in the current path of skill trees, they're also small increment per point investment up to 3 points invested. 

Loot cycle is a mess. People are convinced that certain items are just straight up a myth while others seem to get them at every turn; ideally this would be great for cooperative merchantry where players group up and market their goods they've found to other players, doing 'expedition trades' with one another but personally I don't think that it would go well with the fact that killing others is very easy. So maybe if the developers put in a sort of lobby players could make and join that was a safezone for that aspect it would be much better than current options of just trusting a stranger not to murder you and take your gear for themselves without repercussion.

Enemy types are shallow but can be panic inducing depending on gear and outfitting, I don't really have a lot to say about this aspect, I don't like the enemy that charges and explodes into a corrosive cloud, but that's an opinion I've always had about those types of enemies. There's slight variety due to the rare enemy types and other sort, but the enemies themselves also give very low 'XP', I'm sure this is due to the hoard combat aspect of you'll be killing swathes of enemies when in a group but for solo "In-and-Out" operations as I've been forced to do trying to find very specific upgrade consumables it makes for stagnant level gain.

As for the camp upgrades, this is where the loot cycle and components that just never seem to appear comes down pretty hard. Definitely needs refinement on spawn weights and calculations for players to have at least a little less desperation trying to find things like Hand Planes or Small Cauldrons compared to getting 5 or more blacksmith tongs or crucible/small anvils popping up. Everying requires building supplies and those are very, very sparse as well in terms of quantity spawned and placement where they COULD. I've found them in clothing cabinets. It's weird but I'lll accept any port in a storm when it comes to an essential item like that. It did take until recently, as well, to learn that the camp inventory can be expanded due to poor information and descriptions, so once again, defining what upgrades do as a whole needs to be better considered.

And Finally Item stacks and bundling. With inventory space and stash space being integral to the core of the game, it's genuinely more frustrating to have certain items just not stack. You need ropes and fine ropes for certain things or even to get out at some points of dungeons and they do NOT stack. Ropes taking up a 4 square and fine ropes taking up a 3 column. Not to mention the very small stacks that can be made for other essential items such as building supplies and the various wood types, cloth types, patch types, leather rolls, and so forth collecting any measureable amount of supplies becomes a mess of nesting bags and backpacks that you can't label or name.

With Q4 approaching, I'm hesitant to buy this game if the demo is a reflection as to the current progress state of the game. I understand that studios need funding and have to produce something to maintain that but as it stands, I would not pay money for this product despite enjoying it very much and wanting to play more. This is, by far my favorite game and I have been eagerly playing as much as I can when time allows. BUT, as much as I'll suggest it to my friends and hope to get another person or two to play with, I don't want to see a rushed product from this team.

TL;DR: Game needs more work across several of its systems before I can fully recommend buying into it. Demo is fun, lots of neat things. I like this game a lot. Will change review when notable progress can be seen.

あと敵の中にはこちらに気づくと仲間を呼ぶ敵がいるが、これがちょっと理不尽仕様感がある。このゲームにはしゃがんだりアイテムで隠れるハイドのようなもの、バックスタブが無い上、敵の索敵範囲が結構広い上に後ろにまで伸びてるので、ほぼ確定で仲間を呼ばれる。PTであれば多少盛り上がる要素にはなるがそれでも対処法が無いので割ときついし、ソロだと逃げ一択になるのでそこは何かしら対策をしてほしい。

장점

게임 속 분위기가 매력적이다
어둡고 두려운 미지의 공간을 파밍의 재미를 위해 뚫고 들어가는 그 느낌을 잘 살림

몬스터 웨이브가 긴장감을 올려준다

퀘스트와 파밍의 맛이 생각보다 좋았다


단점

1. 잘 살린 분위기를 단조로운 몬스터 AI 로 인해 많이 죽었다

전체적으로  몬스터들의 위상이 많이 낮음 해골병사들은 뭉치면 석궁의 존재로 무섭지만 
압도적인 포스를 가진 엘리트가 없었고

고블린은 물량과 엘리트가 평범한 수준 오히려 고블린들이 비열하게 접근했으면 무서웠을거같음
독이나 함정을 쓰는 컨셉이였다면 더 긴장감 있었을 듯

오히려 육식종( 한국어 번역 )이 금방 죽지만 제일 긴장되는 종족이였음
빠른 접근 속도, 기괴한 외형, 거대한 질량에서 나오는 압박감 등등
 
2. 파밍의 무의미함

데모 플레이에선 온전한 장비나 물건을 획득할 수가 없어서 파밍시 만족도가 조금 떨어지는 느낌
오히려 장비뿐만 아니라 소모품이나 도구들도 조금 쓴 상태로 나왔다면 
멸망하기전에 쓰던 물품이라 현실성이 더 있었지 않을까 싶음

그리고 파밍 시 도구가 너무 안떠서 데모로 뚫려있는 구간까지 도달하기가 너무 힘들었음
적어도 제작은 가능하게 설계도는 줘야하지않았나 싶음

3. 다양한 무기와 그렇지 못한 실제 사용감

숏 소드, 롱 소드, 도끼, 메이스, 창, 폴암 등등 여러 종류가 있지만 해당 무기간의 특별한 장점이 없음

타격 무기는 갑옷을 무시한다던지 날붙이는 출혈을 유발한다던지 폴암이나 창은 리치가 압도적으로 좋다던지 하는 부분이 전무하고 오로지 디메리트( 공격속도 감소량 증가 ) 같은 부분만 많아서 아쉬웠음

4. UI의 불편함 

상점에서 ESC 를 누르면 팝업창 하나만 닫히는게 아니라 모든 창이 닫혀서 유저의 피로감을 유발함
마우스로 일일히 조작하기에는 손이 많이 가기때문에 이런 UI의 개선이 있었으면 좋겠음

불빛 띄우는 마법 눈뽕 겁나 심함. 진짜 심함. 이거 안 고치면 대체로 부정적 받을 수 있을거임.

가방 안 물건이 상자 수색할 때 멋대로 빠져나가서 땅에 놓이는 경우가 잦음.

퀘스트 보상 등에 적힌 도면이 아니라 다른 도면이 들어옴

고블린 폭탄병 폭탄 너무 자주 빨리 던짐. 아프다기보단 시끄럽고 귀찮음

보인 적도 없는 벽 너머 어딘가의 몹이 날 인식하고 소리 질러서 호드 부름

도면 종류가 아니라 무기 재질에 따라 공격력이 달라지면 좋겠음. 메서 블레이드나 아밍 블레이드 둘 다 똑같이 맞으면 잘리는데 메서 블레이드는 공격력 ㅈㄴ 높고 아밍 블레이드는 공격력이 낮음.

어떤 수리 도구가 어떤 걸 고칠 수 있는지 직관적이지 않음.

마법이 ㅈㄴ 사기고 다른 원거리가 개쓰레기라 아무도 활 안 씀. 마법을 쓰면 금속 방어구를 못 입는다거나 하는 등의 억제 필요함. 활도 버프 좀 하고.

근접 공격 종류가 열상과 관통밖에 없음. 미늘창 직날은 관통이고 도끼날은 열상임. 망치 머리는 관통임. 차라리 열상, 관통, 타격으로 분리해서 각각의 장점과 단점을 만드는 게 나을 듯.

무기 재질에 따라 저주, 정전기, 축복, 소이 등이 있는데, 어떤 효과인지 안 알려줌. 어떤 방식으로든 알려줘야 할 필요성이 보임. 물론 직접 써봐서 알긴 하지만.

마법만 팀킬 되는 건 조금 아닌 듯함. 아예 팀킬을 없애든가, 다른 무기도 팀킬이 되게 바꿔서 난이도를 높이던가 하는게 좋아보임. 근데 이러면 모르는 사람이랑 할 때는 개판날 듯. 

몬스터 정보를 알 수 있는 도감 같은 게 있으면 좋겠음. 코즈믹호러 설정도 보이는데 좀 더 자세한 설정을 알고 싶음. 그리고 어떤 몹이 즉사기가 있는지도 도감 등으로 알려줄 수 있고.

그밖에도 최적화 등 여러 문제가 있긴 한데, 데모 버전임을 감안하면 어쩔 수 없는 듯.

그래도 저 위의 문제점들에도 불구하고 ㅈㄴ 재밌어서 친구들이랑 엄청 했음. 아마 유료로 나와도 어지간히 박거나 비싼게 아닌 이상 무조건 할 것 같음.

Keeping in mind that this is just a demo, here are my thoughts:
The overall gameplay loop thus far is what you would expect from a PVE extraction game in this setting, and it works fine. It's engaging enough to keep you running for more loot; Not too difficult, but with occasional difficulty spikes to keep you on your toes; Just enough fumbling around the map to be frustrating, but not /too/ frustrating so long as you're willing to use outside resources, similar to something like Tarkov. 
This is all working in the game's favor, and makes me hope for more from the final release. 

All that said, the game desperately needs work when it comes to performance, visuals, and general jankery.
I may not be running the most powerful rig in the world, but even with my settings moderated I'm getting seemingly random, massive FPS drops. This, paired with lighting being either non-existent, or blindingly bright in many situations, is really putting a damper on my ability to enjoy the maps that I'm sure the devs have put lots of time and effort into.

At this moment I am going mark this game down as a mild "recommend" if you are someone who is generally interested in extraction games, especially if you need a break from something like Dark and Darker. If these issues aren't address by the time the game releases in full, I'd likely retract that however.

Первое и самое главное. Рекомендую? ДА. Сеттинг, боевая система, система крафта, практически ничего не вызвало нареканий. Единственный минус пожалуй это долгие загрузки, да, местами хромая серверная составляющая. Но это уже надо будет смотреть на релизе в финальной версии. Можно было бы конечно поругать некоторые визуальные вещи, такие как выкрученные в космос ползунки темноты и освещения в некоторых условиях, но это даже какой -то элемент местного антуража, когда даже то, что должно тебе помогать местами больше создает неудобство. Тем не менее яркость некоторых эффектов, Звездный свет, как пример, надо бы убавить. В остальном честно признаться даже не знаю, что можно было бы покритиковать. 

А вот предложить есть что. На данный момент в игре присутствует магия. Но вся она предствлена атакующими заклинаниями в диапазоне от "дать по морде гоблину слегка" до "дать по ж_пе огру и спалить половину города". Нет, атакующая ветка магии на данный момент сделана максимально уместно, тут ничего не скажу. Но что например насчет жрецов и вообще поддержки, как класса? Щиты действующие как дополнительное здоровье или наносящие урон от привязанной стихии, или просто режущие входящий урон. Чары на оружие. Стационарные точки нанесения урона. Магические сумки. При этом, чтобы посох не стал обязательной метой для любого игрока, сделать его основным оружием с запретом на все больше условного короткого и легкого оружия.Руны наложенные на поверхность и действующие как временное ограждение или опять же стены нанесения урона. Что насчет призывателей как класса? В игре есть некромантия. Как минимум в игре есть нежить XD Чисто на мой диллетантский взгляд упускать подобное просто нельзя. 

Еще хотелось бы уточнить про оружие. В игре я столкнулся с ситуацией, когда все решает банальный урон. То есть все сводится к тому, чтобы найти дрын, который просто больно бьет. Но почему бы например не добавить в игру модификаторы булавам и вообще дробящему оружию против скелетов? это же логично. Таким же образом можно добавить топорам и чеканам(крюки на алебардах) пробивание брони. А клинковому оружию дать увеличенную скорость удара, как "более фехтовальному" оружию. Как минимум это заставит игроков внимательнее относиться к сбору под каждый забег, заставляя держать пару -тройку видов оружия под разные ситуации. Аналогично есть предложение относительно "магической вместимости" материалов, когда на одни хорошо накладываются постоянные чары, а другие имеют высокие боевые характеристики и стойкость к износу и повреждениям. 

Возвращаясь к магии, предложение просто уровня qol дать возможность или макрос-кастов, по нажатию одной кнопки или вывод куда-то сбоку свитка с доступными умениями магии. Как вариант можно завязать на предмет во второй руке - от его же градации будет зависеть количество записаных заклинаний. То есть для магии нужны посох, как батарея и условный фолиант, как направляющий элемент. Это в том числе относится к теме баланса, чтобы посох не был просто дополнением к билду, а претендовал на полноценное главное оружие.

Game is good for what they give you, weapon crafting is a little tedious and learning how to repair what feels like trial and error. Combat is good but the hit registry for polearms and how slow most enemies attack makes it kinda like mowing the grass. Lighting is just hit or miss, you either squint at the screen or are blasted by the bloom of floating orbs. Progression is honestly the biggest gripe over stun lock deaths or the ogres one grab insta kill. You have almost zero direction for the endless fetch quests no map markers and no real understanding of the world around you so you flounder looking through countless containers holding (E) for way longer than necessary. The few kill quests are dumb requiring you to slay the worst stun locking kind just to continue a hunt for chalk or pliers so you can finally progress. Quest related items only spawn once on the map making it difficult for friends to progress together. Skeletons need a rework to make them faster or have variations that resurrect them vs them randomly respawning in place making battles more of a time killer than a battle. Magic is way too clunky for actual combat use and the light orb is just annoying. But the biggest turn off in this game would be the few places where instead of dropping down a level you instead die and lose everything...this is a cheap kill and a bad way to design levels, If I die battling a monster thats usually on me but to be stun locked or exploded into a hole is crap. Also we dont need actual PVP in our game world, PVE is perfectly fine and those advocating for PVP should be looked into. Overall I think with time this game will be a lot of fun its just a steep learning curve and a not so forgiving death system.

[h1][b]Expedition: Into Darkness: uma ideia muito boa que ainda precisa ganhar forma[/b][/h1]

Joguei a demo de Expedition: Into Darkness e saí dela com uma sensação meio esquisita, no bom sentido. O jogo está longe de ser uma experiência redondinha, mas é um daqueles projetos que te fazem pensar: "opa, tem alguma coisa boa acontecendo aqui".

A proposta já chama atenção de cara. É um dungeon crawler medieval em terceira pessoa misturado com extraction looter. Você entra nas ruínas, enfrenta criaturas, junta recursos e tenta sair vivo com tudo que conseguiu carregar. E tem um detalhe que deixa tudo mais tenso: a morte é permanente. Morreu, pode perder o personagem e tudo o que ele tinha. Dá pra encarar sozinho ou chamar até 4 amigos pra ir junto.
E o conceito funciona bem justamente por causa dessa sensação constante de risco.

Não é só entrar numa dungeon, bater em bicho e sair com loot e o tempo todo você fica se perguntando se vale a pena continuar explorando ou se já é hora de recuar. A personalização de armas e equipamentos encaixa bem nessa lógica também, e dá pra imaginar um sistema de progressão bem gostoso quando o jogo estiver mais maduro.

[i]Só que nem tudo são flores.[/i]

A demo ainda tem bastante cara de "em construção". Dá pra sentir que as ideias estão todas ali, mas ainda precisam de ajuste fino. Combate, exploração e principalmente o ritmo do jogo pedem bastante refinamento. Em alguns momentos parece que o jogo está tentando mostrar o que quer ser, mas ainda não chegou lá de verdade.

E vale reforçar: isso não é uma crítica pesada. O jogo ainda está em desenvolvimento, então tem tempo de sobra pra equipe lapidar o que já funciona e resolver o que ainda está cru.

O que mais me chamou atenção, sinceramente, foi o potencial. Fantasia medieval sombria + exploração + loot + morte permanente + coop é uma combinação com muito espaço pra criar momentos daqueles de contar depois, principalmente jogando com amigos. A base está montada e a identidade do jogo já começa a se mostrar.

Então minha impressão geral é positiva, mas com ressalvas. Não é um jogo que eu diria hoje que está pronto pra brigar de igual para igual com os grandes nomes do gênero, falta polimento e algumas mecânicas ainda precisam amadurecer.

Mas seria um erro jogar a demo e simplesmente descartar o jogo.

Expedition: Into Darkness está cru, sim. Só que é um cru com futuro. A ideia é boa, a proposta foge do óbvio e tem um potencial enorme pra virar uma experiência bem divertida, principalmente pra quem curte explorar dungeon e jogar em coop. Se os desenvolvedores souberem aproveitar essa base e trabalharem direito nos próximos meses, pode sair daqui um jogo bem interessante.

After every playtest they've released, I've invested the most time into this current Demo - There is so much potential and I'm all for it.. I haven't ever experienced something in this game that's made me want to put it down or say hey this isn't worth playing, and for that I come to appreciate how refreshing it is to have something like EX:ID.  Mixed Reviews are about bugs, or people who don't quite understand the survival curve to this game, and that's okay, but this game deserves much more attention.. 

-Aesthetic and Art: total direction reminds me a lot of LOTR and D&D, really hit the mark on dark, creepy atmosphere that really leaves you wondering what's around the next corner - even with my hours on record, I still have those moments 

-Customization from Character to Weapons: the dyes are a great way to separate yourself from the rest and have an original look, while also being able craft a weapon designed just for you. Plethora of Armors and Gear to truly itch that fantasy itch

-Enemies & Combat : It's came a long way and the current state of combat I'm fine with, and I can only see it getting better and more reactive.  With good gear most weak mobs attacks barely dmg you, where as, a much larger Mob doesn't care and will just pick you up regardless what kind of gear you have - that incites such a fear into me that I do STILL play careful, even fully kitted.  Types of enemies are awesome and well crafted, all 3 types of enemies at the moment feel unique and each play a different way I appreciate that.

-PvE and Coop: Love it, Solo runs are difficult for the reason I stated above with Large units, teamplay is by far one of the better experiences you can have - I don't do runs with less than 3 people, from disconnects to people being eliminated, numbers really don't mean much if you're all not prepared.  I love being able to queue with others, I do wish there was a Designated Host Migration system soo that people can decide to stay in Raid if they want and not extract with everyone when they do, great Risk to Reward factor. A social tab would be nice. 

  This is a game that should receive a spotlight and not be put under the radar, or slandered by reviews who have not given the game the time and patience it deserves.  In the current day of gaming, to have an Absolute 10/10 Gem like this deserves all the recognition it could get.

Edit: Update after another 30 some hours of gameplay.

I was right in some ways with my initial impression, wrong in others. To summarize my early review, I think everything presentation wise about the game is great. Really just needs to generally improve all the features and build out a streamline gameplay loop. My major criticisms are as follows:

1. Solo is doable, but this is mostly because of how the game has an issue with snowballing. Once you get the level of power needed to cut through enemies fast enough, you can mitigate much of the difficulty. A lot of the early difficulty is caused through being overwhelmed (due to not being able to easily dispatch enemies one after another). While I did improve at the game, I'm coming up to the point it feels like my gear has "beaten" the game. I don't really need to dodge or parry, I can chug potions and spam right click to take down most enemies with relative ease. I honestly wish the power scaling as you gear/level up was not as large, as I very quickly went from playing careful and reserved to going full murder mode the moment I realized my actual power level.

2. Progression is frustrating due to RNG. I legit probably spent 30 raids between hitting the Moor / Catacombs hoping for small anvil. Now that I have all the ones I need, they seem to drop like candy.  I'm finally getting to the point that I can craft things (since I was locked out due to not finding specific items to progress my base) but anything I can craft is basically worse than the gear I have now. I get the impression I was supposed to be crafting things throughout my journey, but instead I unlocked the ability to do so 30 hours too late. I'm generally not a fan of the tarkov style "pray you get good RNG and this thing you need drops" quests, the ways Tarkov handles it nowadays with less linear quests would be a good reference towards where things should probably go.

3. As I predicted, things get a bit more repetitive / boring once you figure out more of the game. Once you realize it's all about dodging the special mobs that call in hordes, you've basically figured out the game. It definitely should be a bit more dynamic. Something as simple as enemy patrols wouldn't be a bad idea, or perhaps even having multiple factions on one map to make things more interesting. It's a similar issue to what The Forever Winter is experiencing right now IMO, in that the AI really does just let the rest of the game down currently. Rather than scavenging through a living world, it feels more like I'm carefully running through a WoW dungeon, taking things one pull at a time and ensuring I clear all previous mobs before progressing further.

For the final product, I would hope for more in-depth AI, a cleaned up combat system and a more smooth progression from beginner to seasoned player. (Both in terms of individual player power vs enemies, and the rate at which the player "techs" up.

Very fun game with some "Demo" or Early Access Jank.

Pros:
Lots of loot and things to go through... much of it becomes more useful as you get more schemes and can craft more things
Enemies do come in varieties and they are based on which enemy grouping is on the map.  Swords are great for fleshkin and goblin (particularly unarmored) and heavier, mace like weapons are better for skeletons and many of the armored elites.  Having multiple weapon types is preferred
Progression is slow, hard to find stuff to upgrade your "base" and hard to find schemes, particularly specific ones for items you actually want
Expeditions are as long or as short as you want.  Explore what you want, when you want, and leave when you want.
Quest line is interesting and helps you learn the dungeon.  Biggest mistake I made was not paying attention to the quests and just doing whatever I wanted.  Building supplies, upgrade materials, and a better understanding of the locations of stuff in the dungeon comes from following the quests and reading the dialogue from the quest givers
Each weapon type has multiple different swings that can be controlled by holding leftcntrl, leftshift, or sprinting at enemies.  This allows you to avoid hitting walls and other objects in the way if you actually pay attention and play smart.  It also allows you to aim for enemies with headshots (if they have no helmet) or body shots (if they are helmeted but do not have chest armor) or making large swipes.  You can thrust heavier enemies and perform sweeping attacks against weaker enemies.  Combine this with stamina management and you have a combat system that is more intuitive and allows more control than many of the reviews I've seen have mentioned

Cons:
Combat can be janky.  Game doesn't do a good job of explaining that lacerating weapons are good against non-armored enemies and that piercing weapons are better against armor.  A good piercing weapon (like a mace or hammer) can break armor off enemies and allow easy attacks with swords.  Using both a hammer and a sword as your "1-2 punch" can make a huge difference
Stun lock of enemies AND players are both a problem.  With 4-5 people in the lobby most enemies are very easy to kill.  That being said, with less players in the lobby certain elites can pin you to a wall and just beat the crap out of you until you die... you aren't allowed to move
Pits that cause instant death with no ability for anyone else to recover your gear is a horrible mechanic in a game that makes you lose all gear on death.  Having your teammates unable to recover ANY of your stuff if you fall into a pit or on to spikes is simply moronic
Game needs difficulty levels

At this point, I have finished upgrading my base through the workshop, all of the blacksmith upgrades, and all the weaver upgrades.  I have schemes to make the long-sleeve hauberk, a decent helmet, and some gloves.  When I have those crafted in Damascus Steel my character is nearly invincible except falling damage, regardless of other armor.  Damascus Steel weapons also do so much damage that nearly all enemies become fodder that dies in just aa swing or two, exception being Bog Matriarchs and Crabs that are heavily armored.  Even then, they aren't really threatening with high end gear... they are just annoying because they knock you down.

Clean up the combat a little bit
Clean up the magic usage to function better
Get some difficulty levels that effect what loot you receive
Find some friends to play with and loot faster/share loot and schemes and this game is a blast

It has solid pacing... goes from slow paced looting while boxes "populate" and you discover whats in them and then immediately goes into an enemy blowing horns and summoning a mob of 30+ skeletons + elites that are coming down on you.  Combat in this game is more of a "wear you down" type situation.  You are much stronger than most enemies but finding a reprieve to heal, get stamina, and loot the stuff you want can be challenging. Single enemies aren't threatening but piles of enemies with ranged attacks, knock downs, bleeds, burns, and acid attacks can get dangerous quickly, which is fun.

The game scratches a very particular classic fantasy dungeon crawling itch that nothing else has really done right for me. Being chased by goblins in the dungeons as literal drums bang in the deep, or coming across entire platoons of skeletons in the flooded battlegrounds that all simultaneously turn and point at you is absolutely peak. I've put 12+ hours into a demo, and I've had a ton of fun. I'll address the two primary gripes from other reviews in this as well...

Graphics/Stuttering - Turn your graphics down, that's all it takes. You probably can't run a demo in 8k resolution, big surprise. You can see my specs attached to this review, and I obviously do not have the greatest computer in the world. I get 60+ fps on medium graphics with very little stuttering.

Lighting/Torches - Yes, if you hold a torch in your offhand you have to use a one-handed weapon. That makes sense. If you check your mail in the top right, you'll find a lantern you can attach to your belt, which solves the problem entirely. You can also loot a helmet candle that attaches to your helmet. The issue where the lights reflected too much on the fog has already been fixed.

Overall, I love the demo. The fighting and looting is fun, and there is a real sense of danger from the enemies. Even the basic enemies can easily overwhelm you if you let yourself get surrounded. It seems like the enemies get stronger the more time you spend in a run, as well.

My only real gripes are related to building and crafting. The developers need to make building supplies and crafting tools more available, and they need to make the merchants restock more often. I really haven't been able to build up the camp very much, mainly because I haven't been able to find the supplies needed to do so.

Tricky one to review.
The game is very far away from being ready for a release.

- Crafting (which is a big thing) is totally dependent on finding schematics which drop randomly and the only real way to get the best gear is by crafting it. So you are forced into a grind hell with crazy RNG. Also, weapons are built with few to several dif components and combined to create the weapon - while this gives plenty of possibilities in theory, the system is plagued by the crazy RNG of schematics and the fact that most pieces you add don't really add any meaningful upgrade stat wise or bring anything interesting in terms of customizing the weapon. (you get flat +cleave % / +thrust % dmg etc.)

- The skill tree is mostly not implemented, but the skills are fairly straightforward +stat or %faster this or that.

- Monsters bug out, get stuck and can sometimes just spawn behind you even without a breach. (Breach is a system that spawns mobs.) There's also possibilities of basically getting killed by permanent "stunlock" by attacks that make you fall on the ground. There's also a insta death possibility on catacombs if a mob manages to make you fall into a pit.

- The combat in the game is janky and I mean really janky. You get used to it, but overall the combat feels really unrewarding.

So anything good?

Yeah, the game does offer that sense of danger at least in the beginning. Sadly tho, you quickly realise that there is no danger apart from those few stunlock mobs or getting killed by a bug. The game does have good potential, but there's some major issues it needs to tackle. Mainly the combat and how quickly the game gets repetitive running through the same houses / spots to grind that loot (schematics mostly). The crafting system could be a very cool thing if it didn't require insane amounts of grinding schematics and the dif parts would actually be a thing to really customize how you want to fight.

I did enjoy testing the game out tho and I will keep an eye on it. I would recommend checking the demo out while keeping in mind that this game is very far from any reasonable EA release.

先说感觉吧，以Demo版本为标准

3.防具的选择，和武器一样，防具各个材质也有不同的抗冲击力和元素抗性，比如常见的热处理铁就有50%燃烧抵抗，紫色的发黑钢除了60燃烧抵抗外还有30的酸蚀抗性，但是同为紫色的白银电抗50的同时酸抗是负30，而且耐久磨损速度也不一样，就给了玩家更多搭配的选择，以后肯定要出的负重系统也是压死大全装进图的稻草，毕竟80负重，大全装进图就占了50啊喂，纯PVE没必要把自己搞成铁罐头吧？
4.目前图就2张，没向导摸个十多个小时也能摸个大概，再摸久点小角落、出货点也能摸清，但是图内东西南北是不知道的，而且地图偏黑，哪怕用法杖点了头上的小太阳（甚至体积雾拉最低了那玩意也TMD晃眼！自动选择时候转到眼前我甚至亮到看不到脸前的怪，室内还好点，室外重灾区，最后还是选择提灯），稍微远点还是看不清

Demo Impressions after (15 minutes)

Performance and Optimization:

- The game needs optimization; there was noticeable stuttering at default settings.
- It is not unplayable, but modern players expect smooth performance.
- Early technical polish will be critical for reception.

Gameplay and Core Loop:

- The game presents itself as an extraction hack‑and‑slash with a PVE focus.
- Includes base development and expansion systems.
- Combat feels comparable to Dark and Darker, with slightly less emphasis on passives and skills, but supported by a skill tree.
- Cooperative PVE makes it engaging and potentially appealing to a niche audience.

Style and Presentation:

- My initial impression was “generic” or “asset‑grabby.”
- On closer play, the game shows genuine effort and has a sense of soul.
- Despite the somewhat generic flair, it does not feel like a quick cash‑grab; looking forward to what comes out of it.

Monetization Concerns:

- The studio has no track record, which raises uncertainty.
- Extensive customization options (gear dyes, armor metals, weapon wrappings, buckles, belts, etc.) create strong potential for microtransactions.
- Could remain cosmetic‑only, but there is risk of pay‑to‑win if monetization is not handled carefully.

Overall Potential:

- The game needs more content, but the foundation has promise.
- If the studio proves competent, it could grow into a strong niche title.
- Success depends on optimization, fair monetization, and steady content expansion.

My friends invited me to play this game, and I must admit I wasn’t loving it at first. Performance would tank at times even on the lowest settings, and whenever I was near my friend while he cast a spell, the game would turn into a slideshow.
Over time, though, I became more familiar with the mechanics and started looking forward to jumping in for another session. Thankfully, recent patches seem to have improved performance quite a bit.
My other issues are the lack of polish in some areas, the lack of tutorials, and how RNG-heavy the game can be. 
I went on 10 missions with a friend and never found a single key, including the Blacksmith Key that’s needed for progression.
I’m glad to see the devs releasing patches quickly, and they seem genuinely open to feedback.
I can understand why some people might bail out early, but if you’re willing to give it a chance and stick with it, I think you’ll find there’s a lot to enjoy. I certainly am now.
Awesome demo!

The core itself is good. It’s a PvE extraction looter, with a lot of weaker opponents to fight and a few stronger ones. The atmosphere is great, the controls feel good enough (a bit clunky sometimes), and there’s plenty of loot to gather for you and your party.

However, aside from the usual performance issues that need some optimization, my main concerns are :
- Lack of diversity : I know it’s a demo, but I feel like I had already seen most of what the game has to offer after only one hour of playtime.
- Lighting : You can either have a smaller weapon and a torch, or use a two-handed weapon. Needless to say, if you don’t have a torch, you won’t see anything. And by that, I mean your own torch, because your teammates’ torches don’t help you much.
- Maze-like dungeons : As much as I like exploring these places, I feel like some of them can be really long, and the layouts don’t really help you figure out where the exit might be. Even a ray of light in the distance doesn’t necessarily mean you’re close to the exit. For a short session, that’s fine, but when you’ve already been inside for half an hour, it starts to get boring. Which also leads to my next point :
- Enemies will follow you all the way : Maybe it was just the parties I played with, but once an enemy spots you, it seems to follow you until either it dies or you die. It creates a nice sense of tension, since you’re always on the run, but the lower the player count is, the more tedious it becomes to deal with huge hordes constantly following you around.

So, in short : good ideas, but the gameplay still needs some work. If it comes out soon in its current state, I think it will flop. But these devs can cook if they want to.

I have to admit that the first time I booted up this demo I thought it was bad. However, after that initial play session, my mind kept circling back to it. I couldn’t get it out of my head. So, I decided to give it another chance, AND I AM SO GLAD THAT I DID!

First off, let’s get through the negative stuff first. This demo is essentially an early early access demo. It is rough around the edges. I believe the devs have been up front about this, but it is still something important to know going into this experience. Many of the complaints in the negative reviews are accurate. This game needs a lot of optimization, and the UI needs a lot of work too.

One complaint I’ve seen a lot that I’d like to address is the torch light. I believe the majority of these complaints came from players on the demo’s launch day that played on the map called “The Moor”. From what I can tell, the torch light was interacting with the fog effect on the map and making it very difficult to see beyond a few feet. I think* they patched this already.

I also think some players just failed to read the torch’s description. It literally states that the torch’s smoke can make it difficult to see. The torch is the base level light source you can get, but there are other options you can find, such as a lantern you can clip to your belt for hands-free smoke-free light.

The other problem the game has is that the tutorial simply doesn’t explain enough. The two main things you should know are that

1: you can extract from the entrance you came in through. So, as long as you can retrace your steps you can escape. There are other exits to find though.

2: Block/burn holes when you find them. These are spawners for enemies, and blocking them limits the directions a horde can come from.

Alright, now if you’ve stuck with me so far, I can start gushing about how good this game actually is!

The combat is good! At first it seems clunky, but after spending a little time it starts to flow. Use your parries! For those with gaming mouses, I recommend rebinding the L-shift and L-control buttons that modify attacks to your thumb buttons. There is no lock-on(which I like) so you actually need to aim your swings. You can also control which side you attack from on horizontal attacks be stepping toward the side you want to swing from (at least after unlocking the skill).

This game gets tense. Running out of healing supplies while deep in a run becomes truly terrifying. Especially if you brought in or found good gear you don’t want to lose.

I had a run in the moor where I was completely lost, had a sliver of health remaining, had sacks full of loot, and a goblin horde on my ass, and by some miracle I discovered an extract I’d never seen before. I was seriously running g for my life for 10 minutes straight, and the relief I felt when I found that exit was nigh intoxicating with the endorphin release. This extract then opened a permanent alternative option for entering the moor.

Honestly there are several more experiences I’d like to tell, but I don’t want to spoil the surprise of what you can run into.

The enemies on both maps rotate. During my first lackluster experience I fought skeletons. The rest of the time I have exclusively fought the goblins and the zombies. These two factions of some unique and varied gameplay.

I need to drop into a skeleton match again to see if they hold up. Part of me thinks that they need some work to get the same thrill as the other two factions, but maybe I haven’t seen enough of their units. (Btw, the ppl complaining about enemies spawning under their feet are talking about skeletons specifically. They get reanimated from visible bone piles. This is unique to their faction). If you try a skeleton map and have a bad time, please try another match with one of the other factions. You will be happy that you did.

TLDR: This demo does have some major rough edges, but if you can look past them, your pc can handle the optimization issues, and you fill in the knowledge gaps the tutorial leaves out, there is actually something incredible here. 

Devs, please keep up the good work. Listen to the criticisms, because they will help you make this amazing. However, do not let the more snide reviews get you down. You have something really great here, and I can’t wait to see what else you cook up. (Also, don’t listen to the guy saying that you need a map that shows extract points. I get what you’re going for, and the need to explore and actually find extracts is a good thing imo. You just need to make it abundantly clear that ppl can extract where they entered).

This game has promise. However, I am unsure if I am simply terrible, or if perhaps some tweaks could be made. 
-Agree with the idea of difficulty options or scaled difficulty if you are doing a solo run vs full party
-swinging a weapon, seemingly up to 3 times only and my stamina is drained and I can't even run away to recover.....perhaps separate stamina for weapon use(arms) and running (legs). That's more realistic, also.
-tutorial on weapon builds and how various specs translate for those new to the genre/sub-genre
-voice chat, obviously
-shared party loot, but , at minimu, shared quest/task loot, or a party is just competing against eachother instead of working cooperatively
-option to retrieve gear lost on the map upon death. Not the loot from the map, just the gear you entered with. After three rounds, you have nothing and have to start over. Can help curb rage quitters and bad reviews, I suspect. 
-very inconvenient to have to hit the Esc key to exit the screen when searching for loot. Maybe a right click to exit option instead? Less clunky that way and more immediate defense against approaching enemies.
-easier way to equip gear or armor direct from your bags instead of having to place on the ground and alternate between windows....
-I actually would like the option for target for bow to maybe highlight when ready. It's more of an accessibility issue for those of us with limitations to eyesight. (AKA elder gamers)

Overall, I am looking forward to the full early access game release and to convince friends to join to slaughter some hordes.

The game definitely needs some work in terms of optimization, although thankfully I didn't have any major performance issues on my end despite having pretty decent specs.

In terms of gameplay, I can see the main intended gameplay loop and what the game is trying to offer, and honestly, I'm okay with that. The overall concept is interesting and I can see myself enjoying the loop if the systems around it are developed further.

I do have some issues, though. The talent tree in particular feels poorly designed. I don't really want to see talents that give something like 2% more cleave damage. Those kinds of bonuses can maybe exist as filler or dump stats later in the tree, but they shouldn't be something I'm spending meaningful talent points on, especially when the difference is so small that I can't actually feel the impact during gameplay.

I'd much rather see talents that meaningfully change how a build plays or give noticeable improvements to abilities. For example, talents that modify skills, introduce new interactions, change cooldowns or resource management, or provide significant bonuses to a particular playstyle would make investing points feel much more rewarding.

This game is honestly way more fun than I anticipated.

The very beginning did feel confusing, mostly I wasn't sure what I was looking at in the menus, but after messing around for a bit, I started to understand the preparation loop before going into a dungeon to explore. Had a lot of fun in this game. At first fighting mobs were difficult and intense but once you learn the basic mechanics and acquire gear it gets a little too easy. 

Combat: 7/10 I like the parry system and the directional controls, mobs are fairly predicable. Don't like that there is no reward for parrying but lose stamina, better to just move out of the way.

Enemies: 9/10 almost perfect. Only thing i don't like is being in a corner with a cog doing half my health and slamming me on the ground back to back.

Map Design: 10/10 Destructible environment, hidden buttons, keys, levers, atmosphere, its all great.

Ui: 4/10 Very simplistic, item names cut off you have to inspect everything. item stacks are small

Performance: 5/10 game ran rough until i turned everything on low and only got 50-60 fps, cinematics were still choppy 

Replayablity: 4/10 My biggest gripe is that level up traders takes too long. I have close to 100,000 currency in just a few games and couldn't spend it on anything decent. The quests are unrewarding and repetitive. I spend almost an hour in each raid i go in so a simple kill a goblin type and the next quest be kill this goblin type is rough. And the rep/favor i get after completing a quest is something like .5.

Great experience so far, with a fun gameplay loop. Also love the sword combat.

The game needs some heavy optimizations though, and the UI needs some work.

Overall, excited to see where the devs take this!

[h1] Несмотря на отзывы, игра достойна внимания [/h1]
Мне когда-то очень давно давали плейтест, и там вообще ничего не было понятно. Тут выпустили демку, я посмотрел на отзывы и все передумал качать. Чуть позже посмотрел стрим и все же решил потрогать, как никак демка, ничего платить не нужно.

[h2] Сразу о минусах [/h2]
Да, выглядит она не то, чтобы впечатляющее на 26й год, а даже сложно назвать это неплохо. Она действительно выглядит не очень. Хуже всего, у нее просто отвратительная оптимизация и непонятно даже почему. 
Ко всему этому такое ощущение, что разработчики вдохновляются Тарковым, да он специфическая игра, но назвать его хорошим или брать с него пример - полный маразм.
У игры просто лютейшая нехватка QoL фич, к примеру тут как Таркове, деньги это предмет, и они занимают место на складе. Но самое смешное - я не знаю сколько у меня денег. Нигде отдельно сумма не выводится. Сюда же можно добавить, что я даже не знаю сколько у меня хп или выносливости, нигде подобного стата нет, я не знаю какое суммарное у меня бронирование например и тому подобное. И таких вещей в игре полно.
Не самый приятный порог вхождения. Я не знаю почему в 2026 году, разработчики считают, что абсолютно потерянным новичкам в подобного рода играм позволительно не давать никакой карты. Мало того, что ты вообще не понимаешь ничего в игре, так еще и непонятно куда идти то.

[h1] НО... [/h1]
Игра имеет свой шарм, у нас в целом то лютая нехватка различных PvE екстракшенов. Если вы лутгоблин и в целом играли в подобного рода игры, и вы можете смириться с минусами игры - поверьте, она подарит вам хорошие эмоции в том числе. 
В соло это вообще хоррор лазить по темным катакомбам не зная, что тебя ждет за углом. Спустя пару часов, я понял, что для меня проще всего воевать со скелетами, потому что они не бегают за вами. И тут иду я такой, вижу следующую комнату, там 3 скелета, ничего такого. Я бегу их нарезать, вдруг слева ломается стена и оттуда вылазит огромная тварь. Не будучи уверенным, что я запомнил проход к выходу, я попросту в ужасе побежал роняя кал на вход в данж откуда пришел :D
Да, в игре всего 2 карты, но они очень огромные. Я активно пытаюсь изучить катакомбы, проходов там просто уйма, в некоторые ты просто заглядываешь, выглядит ссыкотно и думаешь как-нибудь в другой раз. При этом приятно открывать новые точки входа, что помогают идти исследовать туда, где тебя еще не было.
В игре абсолютно поехавший крафт. Оружие крафтиться буквально по запчастям: вот тебе рукоять, вот тебе гарда, вот тебе клинок, вот тебе навершие для рукояти. Все это может быть из различных материалов. 
Такое же поехавшее снаряжение. Рюкзак, 2 оружия, поясы, набедренные сумки, штаны, броня на торс, поверх нее можно носить кирасу, перчатки, штаны, ботинки, налокотники, наголенники, подшлемник, защита шеи.

Me descargué la demo sin esperanzas. Empecé a jugarlo y hubo dos cosas que casi me hacen cerrar el juego de golpe: el rendimiento y la interfaz. Al bajar los gráficos a medio, fue mucho mejor. La interfaz es exageradamente fea y difícil de leer, como la de Kenshi o Project Zomboid. Útil pero compleja, nada intuitiva.

Dejando eso de lado, el juego es un extraction de fantasía oscura PvE. Y la verdad es que, a pesar de que el modelado de texturas 3D en la demo deja que desear, funciona muy bien. Los enemigos se llaman entre ellos y de un momento a otro se te puede complicar muchísimo con una horda. El combate es divertido. Falta optimizarlo, pero es divertido. Entiendo que hay daño cortante y punzante. Creo que estaría bien añadir daño contundente para las mazas. Aun así, los enemigos tienen sus debilidades y fortalezas, lo que hace que pienses en qué equipamiento llevar o en que cada miembro del grupo haga un rol.

Cuando luchaba contra los goblins sentía que me enfrentaba a los trasgos de Moria del Señor de los Anillos. Pocos juegos logran eso. O cuando te enfrentas a tres escuadras de no muertos: los esqueletos son lentos pero te agobian con sus armaduras, y los ballesteros de atrás te destruyen. Sin contar con que haya o no un liche. Son situaciones que el propio juego genera y que te obligan a ti y a tu equipo a pensar: usar embudos para frenar la horda mientras el mago castea un hechizo de fuego en área, o correr por la ciudad para despistar a un ogro y que otros le ataquen por la espalda en sus puntos débiles.

Todo eso funciona bien. Los escenarios son bonitos y cautivadores. Los enemigos, aunque quiero más variedad y mejores texturas e IA, son divertidos de afrontar. Podría seguir, pero mejor que lo descubras tú mismo.

Dicho esto, aquí van las cosas que creo que se pueden mejorar:

- [b]Animaciones:[/b] tanto del personaje jugable como de los enemigos. Son bastante arcaicas y se notan poco fluidas.
- [b]Interfaz:[/b] ya lo dije, pero lo repito.
- [b]Más variedad de armas.[/b] El sistema de crafteo de armas con partes mola mucho cuando funciona. Me gustaría ver más variedad, o la posibilidad de añadir runas o filos mágicos para aplicar efectos de estado, o habilidades especiales. Conseguirlo reuniendo materiales podría estar muy bien.
- [b]Mejorar el combate a distancia.[/b] No he visto ballestas aún aunque parece que existen. Mejorar la mecánica de disparo para que un jugador pueda cubrir amenazas peligrosas como chamanes o artificieros sería muy interesante. Facilitar la vida al arquero y la gestión de munición en general.
- [b]Sistema de trampas.[/b] Cepos, trampas explosivas... El juego parece tenerlo pero no lo he visto funcionar. Puede estar muy interesante.
- [b]Mutilaciones.[/b] La idea de que tu personaje pueda sufrir secuelas por heridas graves, obligándote a ir con más cuidado y buscar prótesis, podría añadir mucha profundidad.
- [b]Barricadas y atrincheramiento.[/b] Fabricar barricadas o atrancar puertas daría al equipo tiempo para prepararse ante hordas grandes. Especialmente en niveles cerrados como el laberinto, con sus pasillos largos y habitaciones estrechas, estaría genial.
- [b]Hitboxes y puntos débiles.[/b] A veces golpear o disparar en la cabeza no hace nada, lleven o no armadura. Habría que definirlo mejor.
- [b]Equilibrio de economía.[/b] Actualmente se consigue demasiado dinero y equipo roto, lo que hace que morir apenas importe. La muerte debería tener más peso.
- [b]Más variedad e IA de enemigos.[/b] Que los trasgos compliquen las cosas de verdad: que rodeen, esquiven, mantengan distancia o busquen ventaja, no que se lancen en masa como pollos sin cabeza.

Creo que ya está, seguro que me dejo algo.

Espero que los desarrolladores vean esto y puedan implementar lo que les parezca bien o viable. Y por supuesto recomiendo el juego. Si te gusta Spark in the Dark o el Señor de los Anillos, este juego te va a enganchar.

The game has a lot of potential; making it cooperative PvE is a great choice (I’m not a fan of PvP extraction games).

Areas for improvement:

*   Performance: There are some significant stutters.

*   Loot: Simplify or improve the system; there are too many items, and I feel many of them shouldn't exist.

*   Crafting: Similar to the loot issue, there are too many items, yet basic ones—like rope (essential for camp upgrades)—are very hard to find and cannot be crafted.

*   Enemy difficulty: While the game penalizes you for dying (and it wouldn't be fun to encounter an enemy that kills you in one hit), there should be a way to increase the difficulty of the monsters.

*   Camp immersion: I assume the NPCs will be improved; currently, seeing them as simple avatars and being unable to walk around the camp breaks immersion, turning the time between matches into nothing more than navigating menus.

Hey guys, 

Expedition into Darkness is simply amazing. After over 100 hours in the previous alphas, it captivates me again and again. 

The positives: 

The dark atmosphere. 
You're not held by the hand; you have to figure everything out yourself. Graphics Gameplay, loops, combat system. 

The only negative thing I can criticize is the grind, as it's sometimes too intense. It's unacceptable that you can't find pliers or an anvil even after 20 runs. The devs definitely need to address this. The merchant takes some of the work off your hands, but it's not worth mentioning. 

I can't comment on the performance; the game runs at a smooth 80fps with a 4070ti. It only gets a bit much with hordes of skeletons, but with 200+ skeletons, that's to be expected.

 The crafting and armor system needs a complete overhaul. Currently, it makes no difference whether you have steel or copper armor. There's a percentage advantage with weapons, but I preferred the system from the alpha in January. Overall, there's still a lot of work to be done, but I'm very satisfied. 

I really hope more maps are added. That's all for now, have fun in the dungeon and grinding!

单机联机版+PVE+中世纪暗黑奇幻类型+3D动作砍杀+搜打撤玩法赛道，这些元素组合的战斗搜刮撤离联机游戏可以说相当稀少。

市面上，已有同类型游戏的几乎都是网游，对于不擅长PVP的玩家来说，可以说是一场噩梦。

但从补全单机联机游戏玩法丰富度的角度来说，这游戏挺不错的。

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

但是，《远征：堕入黑暗》的问题出在这个但是上。

1、优化工作做得不好，掉帧严重的问题，这个是最大的。
游戏最基础的是要求，就是能够【画面流畅】+【帧数稳定】的运行。

2、游戏有个完整的框架，但内容方面相当的简陋。
这个问题倒是不大，毕竟是demo，后续开发查漏补缺就好了。

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
接下来，谈一谈我对《远征：堕入黑暗》内容与功能的一些看法与建议：
1、UI界面设计得进一步迭代
血条与精力条颜色得进行区分化设计，让人能够更好的分辨。
像“防具装备栏”，“武器装备栏”，“背包栏”最好放在一个界面上，没必要把“防具装备栏”单开一页。

2、营地设计
希望最好可以设计成一个独立的地图场景。
玩家解锁，升级的新功能设施，可以自由在营地地图场景进行布置，建造。
原因如下：
玩家在对局搜打撤回到营地，应该尽可能给玩家一种“家”的感觉。
而拥有独立场景的营地，就是能给玩家一个更为具现化的“庇护所，安全屋”的感觉。

像仓库这东西，也可以摒弃传统游戏那种只有一个仓库箱的设计思路。
换成生存建造游戏的仓储思路，在营地让玩家自由放置【可以存取物品的家具】。
比如，放十个柜子，在里面存放各种东西。后面存储空间不够，可以继续加存储型家具。

假如开发资金足够，可以让各种战利品模型化，除了放在存储家具里，也可以像【地编】的那种操作模式，把各种战利品摆放在家里，当作一种装饰品。按下特定交互键，就可以直接把场景里的战利品拿起来。
比如：把各种刀剑武器放在营地的地上，挂在墙上，然后靠近按下ctrl营地编辑键，可以选择场景里的刀剑，交互选择收进背包，拿走直接用。如果关闭ctrl编辑键，刀剑就是装饰品。

假如资金有限，那这个思路就算了。

然后就是营地的面积，空间，场景风格，可以设计成阶梯化变化。
比如：
开局默认只是一个破烂不堪的露天篝火营地，能够摆放家具的空间也很小。
第二次升级营地，场景就会变得更大些，篝火也变成火炉，玩家有一个破烂木屋。
第三次升级营地，场景进一步变大，能有更大空间摆放家具，有了屋内与屋外，屋子变成石头屋子。
以此类推，每次营地升级，给玩家惊喜感与成就感。

再营地为核心，向外发散设计一些游戏道具与功能型玩法。
比如，增加种子，可以种在屋外。玩家每次出门，回来以后，植物就成熟。
果实可以加工成食物，食物作为“属性加法存在”。
不吃食物，就是正常难度。
吃食物，就会在持续时间内，为玩家增加额外最大血条与额外最大精力条，为玩家降低难度。

因为搜打撤，需要一个正向游戏反馈，搜来的战利品除了增强自身战力，还应该有一个让玩家可以追求的，具现化的游戏目标。
当然，挑战更高难度，这是一个不错的目标。

但又有谁能拒绝，随着搜打撤带回来的丰富战利品，把自己的营地从一个露天篝火堆，一点点变成越来越坚固，越来越华丽的人类庇护所呢？

（说实在，我有一个不太靠谱的点子。如果可以尽可能降低画面特效与模型精度，是否能允许三十，五十个玩家联机。直接让玩家玩【战地式搜打撤】，再把场景里的所有东西都设计成可以搬运带走的战利品，小东西都揣兜里。家具柜子这类大型战利品，学REPO那种，多个玩家一起抬着，直接上演蝗虫过境，跑得慢的，连土都吃不上。返回营地，可以选择回到房主的营地，也可以回到自己的营地。多人搬运撤离的战利品家具，由最后参与搬运撤离的参与者共有，在结算界面商量怎么分，如果都不想放弃，就摇骰子，谁点大，谁拿走。）

搜打撤这类玩法，能够玩出花的空间，说实在没那么大，如果真照着别家的传统搜打撤模式套用，估计很难出头。

要想走出差异化，那还是得【跨度较大的游戏元素进行拼多多】，如果技术与财力支持，个人感觉如果设计成三，五十人的团队PVE搜打撤，或许是一条能杀出重围的出路。

毕竟，支持三五十人的联机游戏可以向下兼容单人，双人，三人，四人，五人的游戏模式。但如果只有两人规模，是没法向上兼容更多玩家进行联机游戏。非要说的话，可能比较繁琐的是，不同人数联机的怪物密度与战利品数量如何设计会更加合理，这个可能要花些时间设计一个动态调整的函数控制怪物与战利品倍率，让玩家感觉怪物密度与战利品数量都很合适。

Retour sur la démo

> **N’oublions pas que nous parlons d’une démo.**

👍 Points positifs

* **Ambiance :** très réussie. Elle retranscrit vraiment la peur et le chaos, avec un côté qui me rappelle les premiers livres de *Warhammer*.
* **Immersion visuelle :** excellente, même avec les réglages graphiques au minimum.
* **Système de craft :** de très bonnes idées, avec un vrai potentiel.

🔧 Points à améliorer

* **Performances :** grosses chutes de FPS. Sur mon PC vieillissant, je suis à environ **30–40 FPS seul**, mais seulement **10–20 FPS à deux**.
* **Craft :** gagnerait en clarté et en simplicité. Par exemple, pouvoir utiliser directement les objets présents dans les sacs pour fabriquer des armes et des armures.
* **Missions :** certaines sont trop redondantes et ne sont malheureusement pas rétroactives.
* **Difficulté :** c’est un sujet qui fait débat dans mon groupe de joueurs. L’idée est très bonne, mais elle mériterait encore d’être affinée.
* **Variété des ennemis / difficulté :** il faudrait davantage de variété ou de montée en difficulté. Par exemple, même avec une armure basique, une arme à deux mains avec **48 taille / 33 estoc / 0,6 inertie / 80 % fauchage** me permet de traverser les Landes sans vraiment craindre les ennemis.
* **Soins :** permettre d’utiliser directement les objets de soin depuis le sac serait un vrai confort.

### Conclusion

**Une démo très prometteuse**, avec une excellente ambiance et une vraie identité. Il reste surtout des points d’équilibrage, de lisibilité et de confort à travailler, mais la base est vraiment intéressante.
