While the game is still rough around the edges, it's a very fun game. I played the Dec 2025 and June 2026 Playtests, and had sunk a -ton- of time into them prior to this Demo being released. Each one improved on the last, and hotfixes/patches came out nearly daily for a vast majority of these test phases. It's clear that the devs are actively working on improving the the game, and performance. Currently the performance and combat need some refinement, but it's an ever improving work, the Demo's combat is in a better state than the Dec and June playtests, and the performance feels improved slightly as well, I believe they are actively working to fix those issues, so keep that in mind, you may need to adjust the settings in game. 

The potential is there. The ability to pick a weapon suited to a certain playstyle, customize it to your preferences with different material types for visual and gameplay effects is so satisfying, and it scratches that PvE itch that games like Dark and Darker left behind, without the stress of being jumped in PvP, having loot stolen, or having a timer to force me out. 

Days before the Demo came out, I was thinking to myself. "Man, I want to play more Expedition Into Darkness! I can't wait for the next playtest/release." Only to check the store and find out the demo came out to fix that craving. This game had me hooked from my first playtest of it, and have been excitedly waiting for any news/updates since.

Pros: A very satisfying dungeon crawler with a risk/reward system, and bare bones to build on. A large talent/skill system, and armor/weapon customization system that few other dungeon crawler games have. 

Dungeons have rotating modifiers, and mob types. Currently there's 3 main enemy factions, with some factionless mobs that are there regardless of the factions. IE, Animal type mobs, Crabs/Tentacles etc. For modifiers there's ones that will adjust the quantity/quality of loot, the amount of mobs, the weather, etc.

Different mob types have different threats, strengths and weaknesses, the Demo's worked on balancing some of the pain points of some mob types from previous updates.

Them adding new effects to different kinds of metals/items gives that loot goblin in my brain even more reason to keep digging through chests to find that special something for my specific build/weapons/armor.

Cons: As of currently, the combat is a bit simple compared to other loot-extraction games, that may not be a bad thing for everyone, but at the very least there has been an improvement over the last two tests to the Demo, it's clearly a work in progress. Halberds and Spears were near useless in the Dec playtest, and slightly more functional for spears in June, and fully working for both in the Demo. 

The biggest downside is the performance at the moment. It's improved since the June playtest, and multiple hotfixes have helped it in the Demo. If you've got a similar build as my own, you may need to lower the settings down to medium, cap the fps to lower than ideal, and reduce some of the advanced settings like bloom/volumetric lighting, etc. Once you fine tune it, the only fps drops I've had tends to be with spell casts from some enemies, and around mirrors. I've faith that they'll fix these issues as well.

TL:DR. Game's got a great gameplay loop, and huge potential for even more, just needs a little bit of polishing work on performance. Highly recommend!

Performance issues; Stuttering in menus, low fps in areas that change in lighting, low fps in cinematics. 
Gameplay issues; When you swing a melee weapon your character is forced to move forward, pathing issues for mobs, and it is much to easy to accidentally heal an ally when you intend to self heal. 

Recommendations to devs; Some sort of guild option for friends to work together on group projects or buildings. 
A PVP option would be nice, if the maps are procedurally generated and have more random spawns.
Ariel arks or landing indications for thrown items.

Wow. I was not prepared for how fun this is. It's clumsy and has a steep learning curve, plenty of jank (awkward to move, fight, enemies get stuck in doorways/animations) and quite a bit of lag. That out of the way I love this game already and I wish I knew I needed a dungeon crawler in my life sooner. The weapons, armor, and loot are incredible and the intensity of the matches leaves you sitting there muttering "I can't believe I just escaped that." I feel like a long time childhood dream has been fulfilled playing this and even though I'm sick to death of extraction games this was genuinely something new and fresh. Did you like the Fellowship of the Ring? Then you'll love this. It's basically the road through Moria and if escaping a dungeon with hoards of creatures doesn't get you I don't know what will. I can't believe this is a demo.. not early access, just a demo! My mind is blown, the jank is totally forgivable in this context and I can't freaking wait to see the final build. Take my money.

Expedition Into Darkness is a dark horror dungeon-diving game set in an old-world setting filled with mystery, stories, and danger.

You and up to four other players venture into these dark dungeons in search of loot and riches. But every turn can lead you into dark, corrupted corridors filled with monsters waiting to attack.

One thing that really stands out is the freedom the game gives you. You can build your own weapons or buy them, depending on how you want to play. There’s plenty of room to explore, experiment, and create your own way of surviving the darkness.

The development team is also constantly updating the game, which is a great sign for its future.

If you enjoy dark horror, dungeon crawling, exploration, and fighting your way through dangerous worlds, Expedition Into Darkness is definitely a game to watch out for!

Dieses Spiel macht einfach unfassbar viel Spaß.

Ich hatte bisher richtig viel Freude damit, vor allem wenn ich mit Freunden spiele. Ehrlich gesagt besteht ein großer Teil des Spielspaßes einfach darin, die Welt gemeinsam zu erkunden.

Man startet mit:
„Lass uns nur kurz diesen einen Ort anschauen.“

Und irgendwie ist man 20 Minuten später komplett verloren, mehrere Kilometer vom eigentlichen Ziel entfernt und fragt sich, warum plötzlich alles um einen herum brennt. 😂

Die Erkundung ist wirklich einer meiner Lieblingsteile. Es gibt ständig etwas Interessantes zu entdecken, und mit Freunden macht das Ganze noch mehr Spaß. Man kann problemlos mehrere Stunden damit verbringen, einfach herumzualbern und zu sehen, wohin einen das Spiel führt.

ABER …

Das Kampfsystem braucht definitiv noch etwas Arbeit. 😅

Manchmal fühlt es sich weniger so an, als würde ich gegen die Gegner kämpfen, und mehr so, als würde ich gegen das Kampfsystem selbst kämpfen.

Die Grundidee ist definitiv da, aber ein bisschen Feinschliff würde nicht schaden, damit sich die Kämpfe flüssiger und befriedigender anfühlen.

Wenn das Kampfsystem noch einmal ordentlich überarbeitet wird, könnte dieses Spiel noch viel besser werden.

Abgesehen davon habe ich wirklich eine großartige Zeit damit. Die Erkundung macht Spaß, mit Freunden ist es noch besser, und es gibt ständig Momente, in denen man einfach über die völlig absurden Dinge lachen muss, die im Spiel passieren.

Würde ich es empfehlen? Absolut.
Würde ich es wieder spielen? Auf jeden Fall.
Würde ich meinen Freunden in irgendein völlig zufälliges Gebiet folgen, obwohl keiner von uns auch nur ansatzweise weiß, wo wir sind? Zu 100 %.

Kampfsystem: „Wir müssen reden.“
Alles andere: ❤️




This game is just stupidly fun.

I’ve had a really good time with it, especially when playing with friends. Honestly, half the fun is just exploring the world together. You start with “Let’s just check out this one place” and somehow 20 minutes later you’re completely lost, 3 miles away from where you were supposed to be, and wondering why everything around you is on fire. 😂

The exploration is genuinely one of my favorite parts. There’s always something interesting to find, and playing with friends makes it even better. You can easily lose hours just messing around and seeing where the game takes you.

BUT...

The combat system definitely needs some work. 😅

Sometimes it feels less like I’m fighting the enemies and more like I’m fighting the combat system itself. The idea is there, but it could definitely use some polishing to make the fights feel smoother and more satisfying.

If the combat gets reworked a bit, this game could be even better.

Other than that, I’m having a great time. The exploration is fun, playing with friends is even better, and there’s plenty of moments where you just end up laughing at the stupid things that happen.

Would I recommend it? Absolutely.
Would I play it again? Definitely.
Would I follow my friends into a completely random area even though we have no idea where we’re going? 100%.

Combat system: “We need to talk.”
Everything else: ❤️

[h1]Alpha Playtest deutsch/english (Spielzeit: 29,4 Stunden/hours)[/h1]
[u]Update zur Demo siehe ganz unten / Update for Demoversion see at the end of the original playtest review) [/u]


[i]"Die Kapelle ist still, aber standhaft, eine seltene Zuflucht
an diesem verfluchten Ort. Aber selbst hier scheinen die Schatten zu flüstern.
– Bruder Elric, Paladin der Wache,
starb später in den Tiefen"[/i]
_______________________________________

Hinab in die Finsternis...

Der Alpha-Playtest lief - was mein System betrifft - äußerst stabil, auf größere Bugs bin ich nicht gestoßen, das Spiel ist lediglich einmal abgestürzt was ebenfalls bemerkenswert war, wenn man andere Alphas betrachtet (ja, ich schaue Dich an....Star Citizen :-).

Das Spielprinzip ist einfach, es ist ein kooperativer Extraction-Shoo… äh ich meine -Slasher, garniert mit einer guten Portion Inventory-Management, die für mich aber nie
nervig war. Das Gameplay ist hinsichtlich der Charaktersteuerung flüssiger und schneller als z.B. Dark and Darker, was Ausweichen und Springen betrifft. Die Animationen des Charakters und der Gegner sehen natürlich aus und nicht so steif wie teilweise bei - ich muss wieder den Vergleich ziehen - Dark and Darker(was ich übrigens trotzdem sehr empfehlen kann).
Es geht im Kern letztlich darum den Dungeon zu erforschen und immmer besseres Loot zu finden unter anderem auch um seine "Basis" weiter zu verbessern um z.B. dann an der Werkbank mit gefundenen Materialien etwas craften zu können. Auch Questgeber erteilen Aufträge, bei denen man bestimmte Gegenstände finden muss, was nicht unbedingt immer beim ersten Anlauf gelingt und zusätzlich motiviert, den nächsten Abstieg in die Dunkelheit zu wagen.

Was zusätzlich besonders hevorsticht, ist die Möglichkeit seine...Hieb- und Stoßwaffen anzupassen. So kann ein einhändiges Schwert z.B. hinsichtlich Klinge, Griff, Knauf, Parierstange angepasst werden.

Auch Anwender der arkanen Künste kommen in diesem Spiel auf ihre Kosten, die Corruption-Mechanik fügt sich dabei stimmig in das Gesamtpaket ein. Magie ist nichts gewöhnliches und bringt große Macht aber auch große Gefahr für den Anwender mit sich.

Der Artstyle ist düster, die Atmosphäre bedrückend und von lauernder latenter Gefahr geprägt. Schon beim Betreten der Kapelle spürt man, dass man hier nicht der unverwundbare Held/Heldin ist, sondern, dass man sich in etwas hinein begibt und möglicherweise nicht mehr rauskommt - obwohl man es dann meist doch geschafft hat, von den Oberen Höhlen mal abgesehen ;-) Evtl. ist einigen Lesern die Reihe "The Black Company" bzw. "Die Schwarze Schar" von Glen Cook bekannt bei der es um eine Söldnertruppe in einer ebenfalls düsteren Fantasy-Welt geht. Expedition: Into Darkness hat für mich genau diese Atmosphäre, also einer dieser Söldner zu sein, der sich primär auf seine Ausrüstung und ggf. auch Ausbildung verlässt gut eingefangen. Die hierfür verwendeten Stilmittel insbesondere die Andeutungen über Texteinblendung aus Journalen oder Auszüge aus Berichten sind hier auf den Punkt gebracht. Die Kämpfe sind brutal und blutig, wobei auch schon mal Körperteile fliegen, evtl. also nichts für schwache Nerven bzw. Mägen :-)

Die Soundkulisse und stimmige Hintergrundmusik setzt der oben beschriebenen Atmosphäre die Krone auf.

Ich freue mich ehrlich auf das fertige Ergebnis und hoffe das die Entwickler durchhalten.

Was dem Spiel fehlt, und das ist leider oft auch bei anderen guten Titeln der Fall, ist ausreichend gutes Marketing. Ich bin nur - gottseidank - durch Zufall auf den Alpha-Playtest gestoßen. Es wäre eine Schande, wenn der Erfolg nur daran scheitern würde.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[i]"The chapel is quiet but steadfast, a rare sanctuary in this cursed place. Even here, the shadows seem to whisper.
– Brother Elric, Paladin of the Vigil,
perished later in the depths"[/i]
_______________________________________

Down into the darkness...

The alpha playtest ran extremely stable—as far as my system was concerned. I didn't encounter any major bugs. The game only crashed once, which was also remarkable considering other alphas (yes, I'm looking at you...Star Citizen :-).

The gameplay is simple: it's a cooperative extraction shooter... er, I mean, slasher, garnished with a good portion of inventory management, which I never found annoying. The gameplay is smoother and faster than, for example, Dark and Darker in terms of character control, when it comes to dodging and jumping. The character and enemy animations look natural and not as stiff as in some parts of - I have to draw the comparison again - Dark and Darker (which, by the way, I still highly recommend).

Ultimately, it's all about exploring the dungeon and finding better loot and gear, among other things, to further improve your "base" so that you can, f. e. craft something at the workbench with the materials you find. Quest givers also issue tasks that require you to find certain items, which doesn't always work on the first attempt, providing additional motivation to venture into the next descent into darkness.

Another particularly striking feature is the ability to customize your...cutting and thrusting weapons. For example, a one-handed sword can be customized in terms of blade, handle, pommel, and crossguard.

Users of the arcane arts will also find their money's worth in this game, with the corruption-mechanic fitting seamlessly into the overall package. Magic is nothing ordinary and brings great power but also great danger to its user.

The art style is dark, the atmosphere oppressive, and characterized by lurking, latent danger. Upon entering the chapel, you sensed that you're not the invulnerable hero/heroine, but that you're entering dangerous grounds and may not be able to get out — even though I usually manage to escape, except for the Upper Caves ;-) Some readers may be familiar with Glen Cook's "The Black Company" series, which is about a mercenary troop in a similarly dark fantasy world. Expedition: Into Darkness, for me, perfectly captures this atmosphere of being one of those mercenaries who relies primarily on their equipment and their training. The stylistic devices used here, especially the allusions via text overlays from journals or excerpts from reports, are spot on. The fights are brutal and bloody, with body parts occasionally flying, so perhaps not for the faint of heart or stomach :-)

The soundscape and always matching background music add the finishing touch to the atmosphere described above.

I'm genuinely looking forward to the finished product and hope the developers persevere.

What the game lacks, and this is unfortunately often the case with other good Indie-Titles, is adequate marketing. I only—thank goodness—came across the alpha playtest by chance. It would be a shame if that were the only reason if it fails.

review:
总的来说可以给好评。游戏的底层玩法和制作人想表达的内容都非常切中我的好球区，纯PVE加搜打撤的玩法很适合我这种不喜欢与人竞争的玩家。

但目前还是存在很多问题，下面聊一下我遇到的不满：
1.优化不太行，身边朋友都会抱怨不同程度的卡顿，有时游戏会突然进入隔几秒卡半秒的神秘状态，非常影响体验。
2.光影让人很难受，你可以把场景做暗，但光照不能太刺眼。
3.游戏内引导很差，比如法术相关的操作完全没有提示，修理机制也让人摸不着头脑。
4.易用性和UI也有很多问题。例如双击一支箭拆下其箭头和箭羽后，图标并不会发生变化，让人分不清这到底是箭杆还是整支箭；改装界面在安装配件前无法预览属性，配件之间也难以对比差异；此外也没有任务总览界面可以查看所有任务。
5.动作手感有些僵硬，感觉飘忽，不够爽快。
6.初始仓库太小，前期一堆杂物又不知道是否有用，很影响体验。

接下来说一下我的建议：
1.把上面提到的问题都改进一下，尤其是优化部分。
2.好好重新琢磨一下UI，特别是改装界面的设计，提升易用性。
3.如果不想改教程，那么进入训练场后，在屏幕侧边显示操作表、出招表和法术表，并在显眼位置放置几个木桩供玩家测试。

最后聊聊我的私货（
目前技能树很一般，清一色数值加成，不知道是制作组刻意去职业化还是开发资源有限。我更希望看到轻度职业专精——不是强制分职业，而是让专精某系的玩家获得独特的机制奖励，比如盾击、某系列法术增强、弓箭特殊瞄准、提前布设陷阱等等，让每个流派都有独特手感和玩法，而不是千人一面的模板。（剑与魔法题材感觉还是得有点职业才对味）
Demo版根本就是大學生拿專題作品出來的程度，絕對不推薦。歡迎正式版打臉我。

Не заметил как прошли выходные. 16 часов в демке, это что-то новое. Мне понравилась игра: поначалу она кажется неиграбельной, но стоит только разобраться-игра становится простой. Здесь много что нужно дорабатывать, но каркас уже солидный. Мы имеем перед собой пве экстракшен с упором на мили боевку. Хорошая атмосфера, графика красивая. Локации просто пушка: мрачные поля сражений, темные подземелья, покинутые деревни. Интересный крафтинг пух, когда ты из составляющих собираешь себе оружие по вкусу. 
Требуют доработки: 
 - 3 фракции противников, 2 из которых почти непроходимы для новичков. Мы играли вдвоем и нам предлагали воевать с гоблинами и местными зомбями. При отсутствии брони, опыта и оружия, незнанию точек выхода (а карты тут нет. никакой) все заходы были успешно слиты. Как только нам дали воевать со скелетами-мы каждый раз выходили с полными сумками. Они невероятно проще других фракций.
 - Очень неудобная смена одежды или замена факела на щит. Сделайте так, чтобы перетаскивание работало со всеми предметами экипировки
 - уберите лимит склада. Это просто ужас, когда после часового рейда ты тратишь минут 20, чтобы хоть куда-нибудь вместить свой лут. Попытаться найти нужный предмет в этом хаосе очень тяжело.
- пофиксите добычу некоторых предметов. Вначале дают крепления на рюкзак и фонарь, чтобы можно было ходить без факела в руке. За 17 часов я не нашел ни одного такого предмета. А первый щит мне выпал где-то на 15 часу. Базовый предмет для прокачки лагеря-строительные материалы, впервые увидел часу на 13м.
Так что пилите, Шура, пилите. Игра будет золотая.

先说缺点：
1.优化极差，几乎没有什么配置能流畅游玩吧，不过这些年新游好像都这样，何况这是demo，懒得喷。
2.画面拉跨，光影磨人，画面尚且能忍，但光影不行，亮点晃瞎眼，暗的夜盲症。你可能觉得是游戏特色，但这是游戏，首先要能玩。
3.人物僵硬肌无力到像是近战pubg。
4.没有引导，没有地图，比wf还不知所云，下了图除了战斗爽完全不知道该干什么。
再说优点：
1.物资循环有想法，这可以极大增加游戏乐趣和寿命，让时尚小垃圾有用处，让人摸到什么都开心。虽然还有些不合理的点，但整体是正向的。偏硬核，类塔多些，类洲少些。
2.战斗系统有特点，人物动作肌无力，手感差的同时，也独具特色。例如，你可以微操近战是刺击或是竖劈，左劈还是右砍。魔法释放需要小方向预输入，弓箭要一根一根组填等等。这些小巧思在磨人的同时会添加乐趣和成就感，注意平衡即可。
3.可以自由选择玩法，简单来说，就像森林。一个是人步步为营东躲西藏，五个人是欢声笑语没有怪打。
4.改装系统很有潜力，改造武器可以直接改变武器的类型，例如从稿子变成斧子，进而影响到武器的范围，攻速，伤害，甚至是属性。盔甲也一样能该，但远不如武器多样实用。

单人游玩指南：
1前期没好甲之前千万别去跟怪物群打，也别再地图待太久该走就走先攒钱去骑士哪儿买上几个好甲。
2衣柜和桌子出防具，正正方方有纹章在上面的箱子出武器配件和小概率完整武器。
3缺防具直接坟墓初始点往三楼跑一趟至少三五个紫装不说三楼也有三个撤离点刚好摸完就走，三楼撤离点都在上三楼的左边那个门一直走第一个在教堂的某本书柜上的机关开启隐藏门第二个会路过很显眼，第三个在书房需要敲门，书房桌子上超大概率刷钥匙
4关于武器，缺武器或者配件坟墓初始点一路来到牢房区开右边门然后左边是上三楼的路右边有个往下的就是蓄水池，蓄水池箱子全是出配件和小概率武器的箱子，摸完回头上三楼去大教堂忏悔室对面的小房间也是一个刷武器点
5还是关于武器武器伤害大头在刀刃方面摸配件和商店买武器配件的时候推荐找40挥砍左右的刀刃，40挥砍能保证稳定一刀死小怪50挥砍则直接挥砍死两个。另外锻造武器的材料不同也会有附魔但是商店一般不卖，静电：攻击会让怪受到闪电伤害触发硬直，神圣：骷髅克星被此类武器击杀的骷髅无法复活而且伤害翻倍不过刀刃面板偏低紫色行刑刃24点伤害硬是能跟50面板的武器一样一刀死两
6如果任务让你杀某某某稀有怪物而找不到时可以去坟墓三楼大教堂（需要钥匙或者带个火罐炸门）昨晚更新后大教堂最里面必定刷一只稀有怪。地图是骷髅刷骷髅法师，地图是肉尸时是毒巨人和镰刀尸，地图是哥布林时刷哥布林大只佬拿跟树一样的武器横扫三下和抓人，正面护甲屁股没护甲单人没法打，你远程耗他就丢石头伤害一下三分之一血
7关于照明 油灯可要和腰带组合，油灯可以和背包组合，油灯可以和背包支撑木架组合在跟背包组合，背包可以同时挂上两个灯，如果你在冒险中获得了头盔蜡烛那么他可以和头盔组合，游戏最强大的照明来源是法术，去学者哪儿买个法杖和配套的宝石然后装备进图按小键盘左边上下左右键里按下上在按下鼠标左键便完成，可以持续很久切换武器也不会消失
8加加孩子好友一起玩吧，我需要队友

面白い。デモ（体験版？）でゲームの大部分が分かるようになってる。
固定マップに出撃して素材や装備を拾って脱出する中世モチーフの三人称アクションRPG。
落ちてるオブジェクトが変わったり、出てくる敵が変わったり、異変が起きてたりする。
死ねば身ぐるみはがれるのはとてもエクストラクションゲーム。
マルチで自分含めて5人で冒険出来る。PvPはないが遠距離攻撃と魔法にFFがあるので注意。
製品版がどうなるのか分からないが、デモでは入った所から脱出できるので他のエクストラクションゲームよりかなり優しい。出口も今の所固定で今回はここからは脱出できない等もない。もちろん取り合いもない。
不便だった部分が改善されて更に遊びやすくなってました。開発に感謝。

武器のカスタマイズが豊富で、刃を変えたり持ち手を変えたり片刃を刃物、片刃をハンマーにしたり戦闘中武器を回して使う面を変えたり出来る。今はそれほど意義を感じないがきっとよくなる（期待）
攻撃も3種類あって狭いエリアだと通常の横振りでは壁に当たって攻撃出来ない事もあるのが楽しい。
敵のアーマー部分ではダメージが入らなかったり、重い武器だとアーマー吹き飛ばしたり色々ある。
魔法も杖に宝石を付け替える事で唱える魔法系統が変わったり、複数の詠唱を組み合わせて魔法が出そう。（推測）間違えた詠唱でランダムで魔法が出るのも面白い（自傷はなくなった？）。詠唱がキーボードの十字キーなのでマウスから手を離さないといけないのはコンフィグでカスタマイズした方が楽かもしれない。レティクルがないのでほぼ勘で狙うことになる。自動で飛んでいく魔法もある。楽しい。鍵かかってる扉にイライラしたことないですか？このゲームには”答え”があります。

雑魚敵は基本苦戦しないが、敵を呼ぶモンスターが現れてL4Dみたいなラッシュがくるとソロでは押し切られる場面もあって面白かった。クロスボウがしっかり怖い。ナイス中世。でかい敵は中々に迫力がある。

ダンジョン探索に時間制限がないので、自由に探索できるのがとても良かった。空腹やのどの渇きも（今の所）存在しない。拾えるアイテムも豊富でごみ漁りが捗る。バッグインバッグも可能で肩に食い込む重さで生を実感しよう。落ちてるアイテムも強調表示でわかりやすく、PUBGで画期的だと思った付近に落ちてるアイテムをインベントリ画面でリスト化して直接カーソルを合わせなくても拾える神機能がついてる。これだけでこのゲームをオススメしたい。レビューも書いた。

デモが公開されて数日で更新がはいったり、このレビューが参考になるかは怪しいがうちのPCスペックでは設定をかなり下げてプレイしても重いシーンがいくつかあった。製品版では最適化に期待したい。

また、デモゆえ説明不足な点も多いためある程度察する部分も必要だった。武器鞄タブと防具タブが別なのでドロップした防具を付け直すのにひと手間かかる。ランタンの使用方法がベルトか鞄のカスタマイズでつけるの説明がなかったり、ランタンをつける位置で逆光になり何も見えない。レベルが上がると取得できるスキルの効果が分からない、寝袋ってどう使うの？など。製品版では諸々改善されてることを期待したい。

マルチでPvPにすると対戦相手がいないと困るからマップの回転率をあげるために制限をつけたり既に漁られたマップに投下されたり、NPCをおざなりにしたり戦闘が起きやすいように誘導されたり窮屈になりがちな部分が解放されてとても遊びやすくなってる。対人のひりつくイレギュラーは起きないが、そういうのを求めてない人にはデモの時点でオススメ出来る。PvPvEに慣れてる人には物足りないかもしれない。

既存のエクストラクションゲームに酷似した部分も多いが、気になった人はぜひ触ってみて欲しい良いデモでした。

Tbh, as a German, I don’t really get the criticism from people who have barely played the game for an hour.

Does the game have its flaws? Yes. Performance sometimes drops in certain rooms or when there are masses of enemies, but that’s kinda the whole point of a demo. Through the demo, they can get feedback on performance and work on it, just like with the combat system or other things people are bothered by.

I don’t want to give the game too much credit because I do think the maps can get tiring pretty quickly, and once you have armor, the game becomes kinda easy — even against giant crabs. Not to mention that playing in a team is basically a walk in the park.

But I absolutely love the idea of an extraction game with knights, bowmen, mages, etc., combined with a dark medieval aesthetic. You gotta respect the effort and the ideas behind it, because this game has something I really miss in other extraction games (except maybe ARC Raiders): **people actually being kind, supportive, just enjoying the moment, or helping each other out.**

In Tarkov, for example, people would probably bully you just for breathing wrong. 😂

That kind of community interaction is honestly one of the things that makes this game stand out to me.

A lot of potential. I've been excited for more purely co-op extraction games since I'm old and don't have the mental energy for PvP trolls these days. I do recommend checking it out, but the demo itself has a lot of issues. I'll list my 4 biggest issues:

1. You can't see item stats before you buy them from any merchant. 
2. The game (at least afaik) doesn't a beastiary or codex where you can eventually learn about enemy strengths/weaknesses in stepped tiers after defeating enough of them or something, which would be nice as opposed to hoping the loadout you took will just "work good enough" for what you're fighting.
3. Performance is all over the place. I've got a decent rig and I was anywhere from 25 FPS to 80 FPS.
4. If your game crashes (it did a little, not a lot), your entire loadout is lost, even if you're still in the main menu/lobby. Strange bug, I'm sure.

Anyway, cool game, lots of potential, but the finished product will need some work to be great.

Game is fun despite some jankiness with matchmaking and inventory design. The actual gameplay of running into hordes of monsters and freaky bosses with your buddies is usually top notch and stands out from other fantasy extraction games, so there's lots of potential for the future.

The game feels really unpolish and need more time in the oven. Hordes of enemies sometimes spawn right in front of you. Enemies can be seen wearing an armor and disappear from their body the moment you kill them. Animations are janky. Skill trees are largely unimplemented even the basic ones. Performance is horrendous and will hurt your precious GPU. The only bright spot is how large the map is and gives you a good sense of exploration.

First, my one and ONLY complaint (outside optimization), a total lack of any sort of map. Why is this an issue? You play in a pretty open environment filled with monsters, and poor visibility (fog, dust, smoke, etc. in game stuff...intentional). This makes finding/seeing things difficult. Makes it challenging, forcing you to push forward slowly, methodically. However, with a lack of a map, everything kind of blends together quickly. You get neither the option to "draw" your map as you explore, or given one that gives you points of reference to know where you are going...as in most other games of this nature. This creates the feeling of artificial difficulty for the game. And it creates a high level of frustration when you die when you can't find the exit.

Outside that, the game check ALL of the boxes for me. PVE, challenging game play, extraction, solo friendly-ish, coop play, NO pvp. It is a game that I was really looking forward to, and still am to be honest. I just wish some sort of mapping feature would be here.

Definitely going to have to "get gud" before I am successful here.

After spending 11.6 hours with this demo, I can honestly say I've enjoyed it more than some AAA games I've paid £60 for. I can't wait to play more. Out of curiosity, I checked the reviews afterwards, and I was genuinely surprised by how negative many of them were.

I also played during the open beta, and the game has come a long way since then. Back in the beta, I thought the core concept was fantastic, but it wasn't in a particularly playable state. The improvements made since then are obvious.

One of the things I enjoy most is that the game doesn't constantly hold your hand. Too many modern games tell you exactly where to go and what to do, which, in my opinion, takes away the sense of discovery. In these 11.6 hours, I've only been playing on the first map, learning where items can spawn, remembering key locations, and figuring out the best routes for quests. It genuinely feels like exploring instead of simply following markers from objective to objective.

I've played both as a trio and as a duo with friends, and we've had a great time. Customising equipment, searching for different attachments, and browsing the shops all add to the experience and give you plenty to work towards.

Considering this is only a demo, I'm seriously impressed. If the full game launched tomorrow, I'd happily buy it. My PC is getting pretty old, and I can't afford to upgrade it right now, but the game has been completely playable for me. That's more than I can say for some recent releases. For example, I played Hunger for less than 20 minutes because it was plagued with performance issues on my system.

I'm also not a huge fan of Unreal Engine games. To me, many of them have a similar feel and suffer from the same clunky movement and gameplay quirks. That's a personal preference, but it's one reason I appreciate what this game is doing differently.

The combat could definitely use some refinement, but this is still a demo. That's exactly the kind of thing I'd expect to improve during development, and the progress from the open beta gives me confidence that it will.

If you're looking for a game to jump into with friends without knowing much about it beforehand, I'd absolutely recommend giving this a try. It's been a fun, challenging, and rewarding experience.

As for the complaints about there being no minimap, I honestly don't understand them. You're playing as a person in a medieval setting—why would you have a GPS-style minimap and compass pointing you to every objective? If anything, I'd love to see physical maps as lootable items. Imagine finding a map during a run, bringing it with you, and marking it yourself. I think that would fit the game's atmosphere far better while still giving players a useful navigation tool.

I feel like a lot of people are currently overlooking that this is a demo and has been out for three days, so bugs, breaking and so on have to be expected. 

Generally, it is an incredible game and there's a lot of fun to be had. Maps rotate enemy types and such similar to effects in Arc Raiders and the looting system also has parallels to that game's. You actually have to take enough into the dungeon to survive, loot and (hopefully) thrive whilst also balancing out the amount you take so you don't lose everything. Even after hours of playing, myself and a mate were tricked into underestimating some enemies and paths and had genuinely good fun.
Upgrading and levelling feels intuitive and happens as one goes without becoming a nuisance. 

Optimisation-wise, the game runs okay but will need a lot of work to actually run on mid-tiered systems with decent settings, I espcially noticed RAM and GPU usage spikes during gameplay, with the game eating up to 14gb ob RAM at times which is impressive in its own way. 
Crafting is very open and I love that but I honestly feel like sometimes it makes no sense in regard to the rareness of an item. You have a blue blade doing 56 dmg base and the same one in blue doing 30 or 32. 
Inventory management is funky but definitely needs ui work, as with quite a few things. 
I love the skill tree and skilling allows for a group to specialise and adapt a lot better than in other games, so that is also a massive plus - maybe a skill similar to Lone Wanderer in Fallout could be implemented for solo players and auto deactivate upon a player joining a party of having someone join. 

That's all for now - the game is good fun and some people seem to not fully understand what a demo is, hence the mixed reviews. 

Keep it up devs, it's really fun!

Nada.

Nada.

This is my 100th game review and i chose this game because i feel like its important. I've played 30 matches and so my review might hold up better than those that just started and dropped it.  

Let me begin by addressing the outside game dramas of this community which will NOT effect the final score of this review but extremely important so everyone should know prior to playing. The fanbase is small, yet extremely elitist, they have not only flooded artificial positive reviews to balance the score but also actively have went on a campaign to give negative reviews the ''funny'' reactions. Most of these people dont want change, they want extra features on top of broken glass, they want even further convoluted historical accuracy in a game about magic, skeletons, and zombies. Ideally, a side note is that i was in the discord previously, asking simple questions will resort in others asking for you to self doxx your entire location and name to them for feedback. And let me end this segment by saying the devs are willing to improve the game, 1 patch seemingly every day, however is heavily misled by their own community and perhaps by themselves as well. These negative reviews should be listened, taken into account and always taken seriously, period. And let me remind everyone that this is a DEMO not a PLAYTEST. 

For reference: 
Playtest: Pre-Alpha - Late Beta
Demo: Segmented Full Game Experience

This has been the industry standard for over 40+ years. Reference the Mortal Shell 2, and Onimusha demo. 

Game Review
--------------------------
The game itself is oddly addicting and extremely fun.... when its working, which is extremely rare. Theres a few examples of how bad this game can get and ill reference one of my own experience. Theres a system in-game where you can catwalk across a small board from point A to point B and spikes are below, classical dungeon trap. However what the game doesnt tell you is if you accidentally do it at the same time as someone else youre flung into the spikes below (this is a instant kill and thus you lose absolutely everything). 10 hours of grind i had on my character simply gone within seconds because of extremely bad collision coding and the lack of delayed prompts. Another example is if three hordes is spawned in a matter of a few seconds in close proximity your frames drop by a whapping 30 to 40 frames, this could be easily fixed by lowering the model impact on the system and model itself via less detail and less mass which is rudimentary at best but instead they've decided to give every model and asset in the game a heavy load thus causing frame issues which is also a very well known issue with the engine theyre using. 

Lets move on to the most convoluted loot and inventory system ive ever seen. It seems like the vision is completely in limbo between wanting to be high historical and high fantasy and the direction is stuck between those two seemingly as if in utter confusion and without real direction. For example - youll have historically accurate named helmets, pieces of gear, and pieces to attach to that gear but unfortunately i dont have a masters degree in medieval history so im completely lost to what goes with what so i have to needlessly spend money on things on a guess. If they wanted to keep historical accurate names then also add a prompt to what it goes with, otherwise id like to see them remove all historical accurate names in the game because casual players like myself dont know what a ''whatachikaboomboom'' helmet is and ideally dont know that the ''belatachikawow'' visor dont go with it. This is a game about killing zombies and goblins with optional high fantasy magic.... just name a hammer a hammer and a sword a sword. 

Currently there is only 2 maps, however it seems like theres truly only 1. The Moor map in comparison to the Catacombs is vastly more enjoyable and 100x bigger than the Catacombs is thus leaving experienced players no choice but to pick the Moor because whats the use of picking a small map unless youre solo. To find a match on either is extremely punishing on its own due to the fact that when you matchmake your map changes automatically by itself to match the host..... why? And whats the purpose of choosing when itll just change anyways? 

The enemies are extremely unbalanced, goblins being extreme difficulty, skeletons being hard difficulty and the fleshkin being super easy. And you might be asking whats makes it like this .... the archers... each arrow that is shot by one of them takes HALF of your entire health bar regardless of armor rating... thats ONE archer, some groups have 2 some 1 but the hordes are often and will spawn literally in front of your face. The fleshkin luckily has no archers but they do have the most brutal minibosses which sometimes seemingly never spawn and sometimes spawn 50 times a match, theres no in-between. 

--------------
Overall the game is fun when it works and theres TRUE promise in this game but lacks actual experience in its execution; a team seemingly thrusting head first into the cockpit of a boeing 747 airplane with a bachelors in english. A overly ambitious, poorly made mess that could be good with the correct guidance yet falls heavily on its face without one. A game that wont survive without a complete revision especially with the looming threat of Blight: Survival nearing its horizon at the exact same time this game is planning its own release which is grossly incompetent seeing what theyre providing now. 

~ 6 / 10

Finally, the gameplay gets extremely stale after a few hours - you end up running the same basic looting runs 10x in a row to find a crucible/hand plane. Additionally, performance seems to have gotten worse from the playtest and enemies have a worse hit recoil like fencers.

Suggestions: Have some procedural generation for maps like have the layout change slightly between runs or at least have containers move around, have difficulty modes that increase or decrease loot chances, and have much stronger enemies like minibosses that sometimes guard key locations so u have to fight them or go loot elsewhere.

In the first beta they released, many months ago, I spent more than 10 hours playing with two friends. And back then, the game was missing countless things that it finally has now.

It’s a difficult type of game to get into. But once you’re in, it has everything you need to get completely lost in it for dozens of hours.

Playing it alone is complicated, not impossible, but definitely complicated. The lack of PvP also works in its favor. It makes it clear that the game is focused on cooperation and atmosphere, rather than on who has better loot or who has played more hours than you. Personally, that makes this kind of game much more enjoyable. You get to experience it without the stress and frustration that often comes from competing against other players.

The mechanics, and the fact that the game keeps so many of them secret, will work against you at first. That’s why the best way I’ve found to enjoy it is with a band of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ called friends.

You have to let the game kill (teach) you. Experiment with it. Test its mechanics. Explore. Remember what you’ve learned and try again.

Over time, you start figuring things out. You learn that certain enemies have weak points. You discover that some weapons have special attacks that make hitting those weak points easier. You find all kinds of items that can be used in different situations. And, most importantly, you learn that you have to use your head, because this is a game that will not forgive you for making a mistake.

All of that becomes much more entertaining, and much easier to deal with, when you have friends to play with who are also willing to experiment and genuinely try to understand the game instead of immediately judging it.

That said, the game still lacks a lot of polish.

**BUT** the gameplay loop and mechanics have already laid a solid foundation for something that could become a great game. Perhaps even one of the great medieval extraction games.

And, if you haven’t noticed, there aren’t many of those. We need a few of them to step up and really make their mark.

Give the demo a try with some friends. If you’re brave enough, and have the patience, playing solo is also an option.

I genuinely think this game deserves attention and support. Its developers have something here that could become really special, and they deserve the opportunity to see how far they can take it.

Whether they actually manage to turn it into something great or not, we’ll see.

But they have to try.

They’ve got something big on their hands. **If you know what I mean.**

--Demo Initial Review - 08AUG236--
BLUF: Worth some time with the boyz running through the dungeon and grabbing loot. We played 5.5 hours in one session and we enjoyed it. There are qwirks and issues, but it is a demo and will be early access.

First off, the Nay-Says. Anyone 'not recommending' a demo with under two hours is being an over-dramatic whiner.  The experience is free and the multiplayer is rather solid, stable, and fluid.  If the complaint is optimization, I suspect they have programs open other than Discord for comms.  A demo will rarely be optimized to perfection.

Game is fun for now, excited to see it grow, and I think it is what the market wants to see right now.  A PvE experience that is not too serious, but at the same time has a lot of function built into it.

Some ideas to look into for the release of the game.
5 Easy Wins:
-Reduce quality of starting equipment: (likely a demo thing) make players climb to get armor and components.  Due to the starting weaponry in the demo any green weapon component is not worth keeping.  All the starting equipment is stronger.  This hurts the weapon smithing of your game which should be a core feature.
-camp build up needs to be easier to get the initial buildings: there are lots of initial buildings with items that are hard to find or take a while to gather.  I would recommend opening up these features sooner and then the upgraded buildings always have a mechanism to craft the requirements along with finding them.  Reality is this system is likely already employed, but I cannot find a Hand Cart, Crucible, or Tongs to change how I feel about it.
-Shield Bash: if we have a shield let me bonk with it.  If I should be putting up my shield and hitting “F” to have it happen, this does not feel substantial. Please give us a nice shield swing, the swing and effect could reduced by each enemy hit because that makes sense, if this is a pre-planned skill unlock that is acceptable, if this is an unlock let the next node be an added stab or swing of the weapon as well.
-special/ rare enemies drop loot for the whole team: I think any special enemy should be lootable by all players in the lobby. Can adjust this to be all players that dealt damage.  
-better exit notification/ signaling: I have only noticed signs saying camp once in 14 hours of play.  I think this needs to be more noticeable and maybe the HUD shows a banner on the top saying when players are in an exit zone.

5 Recommendations:
-navigation and cartographer nodes later in the dungeoneering skill tree- not only should knowing which direction you are going (like a heading tape) but making maps after the skill is gained, only allows that player to view map after exploring areas.  This would help add a specialized perk to a player in the group wanting to be the guide/ navigator.
-Vendor Reputation growth +0.01 when you buy 4,000 or sell 1,000.  To prevent exploiting, once items are bought or sold, they are marked with all merchants for given reputation. Could even put a limit on how much reputation a player can earn through trade per round back at the lobby.  Or for every 10 enemies killed on the map with playtime being 20 minutes or more gives you the ability to earn .01 reputation through heavy trading.
-traps should come with ambush parties: a trap goes off should create noise and there show be enemies that rush to the location to fight whatever is there.
-stats page or better tool tips: for armor and more info on different materials and the hardness/brittleness factors. These concepts are not really explained and it takes the player diving in to even see these words.
-inventory white noise: make small one-slot crafting material fill up a bank reserve for crafting. Do not make the player dedicate inventory space to one-slot rags, scrap, etc.  if you let players bin it up to a cap, it will feel better.  Raise resource cap through certain camp buildings.

5 Items on the horizon (probably planned in concept to some degree):
-More enemy sets: (Likely planned) Beastmen and Demons: just more enemy types to help make the enemy population feel constantly different.  Demons would have fire magic, maybe a taller demon with a great sword, maybe some teleportation effects. Beastmen would have more spears and axes, javelin tossers, and Minotaurs.
-module dungeon, with specific hazards on each branch: depending on a map sequence number there will be 2 of the 5 entrances to go deeper into the dungeon.  This will require time for players to find the appropriate entrance, then go deeper, creating further risk to survival as there are only two ways out.  Knowing which entrances are open may make getting out easier.  Each connecting segment to the lower dungeon would have a specific hazard or puzzle players would need to overcome. Could even make the branch players take get locked out forcing players to go through and locate the second branch to get out successfully.
-expanded unit rosters for factions (Likely Planned): Imagine necromancers, bone spiders, and shielded goliaths for the skeletons. Imagine  war dogs, gob-throwing trolls, and goblin sneaks waiting to ambush players from the ceiling for the goblins. Imagine corpse centipedes, chimeras, and bile throwers for the fleshies. Depth in the unit roster equals variable of play that keeps players engaged. This creates stories of success over the monster or running away out of fear.
-Special events that derail player objectives or suffer map effects for hours: imagine players enter trying to get to location ‘X’ to find items that appear there at a high rate.  Upon entering the map there are slight indications of the special event. Passing the wheel on the Moor they see a green glowing tower shrouded in shadow.  As an example The necromancer tower must be destroyed/ the necromancer must be killed during his chant or else the group suffers a blight.  This blight would affect all maps for an hour for each player in that lobby. Or it continues until player rally to defeat whatever is sustaining the effect. The blight effect carries to other people’s games if one person has the blight. The Goblins could have a war party and siege engine that they are rolling across the map slowly. The Fleshies could be feeding an abomination that fills muscles and flesh over a giant skeleton. The blight effects could range from timed waves of enemies, more enemies on the map, higher occurrence of rare enemies, enraged enemies move faster, or exits are reduced to one.  The rate of occurrence could be 20% so it is not on every map, and there could be more generic events as well. Leaving the map (or game) without settling the event conveys the blight on all players that were in the lobby as well.
-More MAPS! (Obviously planned): The Moor has a lot more in it than I saw at first.  It is rather expansive, but there are needs in filling it with events or more depth to the "dungeon" aspect.  Catacombs is a great evolution over what the game originally showed as the dungeon. Keep creating fun maps! Examples of more themes could be: destroyed farming/ fishing village, Desert hideaway (bring on the snakes and scorpions!), a hilly forest (bears and wolves), Derelict Dwarfhold, an ancient tomb, and potentially enemy faction themed areas as boss sites.

This Demo is supposedly version Demo 1.0.1 but it plays more like Pre-Alpha Proof of Concept of an Idea 0.1.0.
But first off: It's free so you can just try it out for yourself and make your own opinion. The Demo seems to have LOTS of missing features, but nothing blocked out from the Demo. Seems like you can just play all you want with no limitations on the implemented features.

Overall, I have taken ♥♥♥♥♥ that were more polished than the current state of this game. Everything visually clips through everything, stuff gets stuck everywhere, invisible barriers, graphical elements constantly visibly popping in and out during gameplay accompanied by stutters, absolutely garbage tutorial that doesn't explain anything, the UI is terrible and overlapping, the animations are just unchanged UE stock, confusing maps and so on. It's all round incredibly janky.

But despite all of this, as other reviews have mentioned, this pile of ♥♥♥♥ has a gem hidden deep inside... (But currently it's a tiny ring gem in a cistern of ♥♥♥♥.)

Due to the jank, the game is VERY easy to win, to the point where when I played with other players, not once did I appreciate their presence and the game never needed any kind of cooperation out of people. A player with a 3 digit IQ can just win against pretty much anything the game throws at them. So despite being co-op, I wouldn't say it's particularly suited for co-op. (Maybe if you and your friends are less competent.)

However, overlooking the jank and figuring out the game's features left me with a fun playthrough of an extraction game without PvP in a grimdark setting. I really liked the enemy types and the music during gameplay along with the feeling of getting whittled down slowly, bit by bit as you need to press on in order to have a chance of escaping. Along that I also liked the weapon crafting - even though it is quite unbalanced and not explained.

The game currently has 3 distinct enemy "factions". Goblings, Fleshlings and Skeletons. And each of them works differently. Goblins are your run-o-the-mill basic enemies. Fleshlings are more susceptible to bladed weapon while being these grotesque nude-ish humanoid figures that quickly rush you down. Skeletons on the other hand are more susceptible to blunt weapon damage but unlike the rest, skeletons only ever walk towards you. But there do tend to be a lot of them at once.

Hearing the audio kick-in after I get noticed and a horde is called my way feels great because with the confusing layout of the maps gives a feeling of claustrophobic uncertainty.

Just because you came in through a specific hallway doesn't mean a horde can't spawn from that direction as well so you need to keep vigilant of your surroundings throughout the match to not get killed. (Some enemies deal a LOT of damage in one attack, especially if you decide to go in without armor.) However you don't need to engage with the enemies. If you think you can, you can try to run and try a different route without killing the enemies. But running does have a tendency to bite you when you round a corner and see a very sizeable horde of enemies you ran from coming towards you.

You can track items you need and seeing the only way to get some of them is by searching through every nook and cranny takes a while during which the enemies will get chances to whittle you down as your inventory fills up and your encumbrance slows your stamina recovery, making extended combat less feasible.

You will go through the map and gather some of your tracked items, but then as your inventory space dwindles, you come across a very good piece of armor which you can't equip during a game so you must make the choice of what to leave behind as carry space is always in short supply. And needless to say, once you find your cool items, you don't get any glowing checkpoint or marker somewhere. You need to figure out which path you didn't take yet and hope that you reach the camp before the game whittles you down bit by bit so it does make for some enjoyable, tense moments.

There isn't much mechanical variety to enemies but over my playtime, the game did surprise me with a new enemy every now and then which was fantastic and brought forward the shrouded mysterious world of the game. (None of them were particularly difficult to beat if you understand how the game works but it certainly keeps you on your toes when out of the darkness comes a... Thing... you've never come across before.

Overall, the game has a TON of terrible aspects shown in the demo and the animated scenes shown on the Store Page aren't very reflective of what the game is like in my experience. It's similar to the Risen remake demo. But I do truly hope that the game does build upon the potential it holds inside by release and it could really be a very good game.

TL/DR: I believe this game has some serious potential. And while it is VERY rough around the edges, I can see it turning into a mainstay for those who enjoy it. 

The overall vibe reminds me of a Medieval version of the Forever Winter. Another PVE Extraction game but set in a post apocalyptic sci-fi setting. Expedition has a very grimdark atmosphere that I feel they nailed right off the bat. The lore such that it currently is at the time of writing makes you curious to discover more. Whether that be in-game or searching wikis. 

Combat feels solid. Swinging your weapon or shooting you bow feels smooth yet still grounded. Mobs feel difficult but fair with enough skill and positioning. This is also one of the few games that has mix ups to your melee feel necessary but not annoying. 

As far as what I'd like to see fleshed out:
-More Lore! I'm a lore junky for sure. Adds depth to games and gives me a reason to keep looking for more.
-A walkable hub. Somewhere to see your progress, gear and party members. Perhaps the training grounds could just be extended to include more features. Would definitely be a cool and immersive addition.
-Permadeath Adjustment. Now for this one I know I am biased towards games not having permadeath so this may not resonate with the Devs vision or other players. But I would like to see 1 of 2 things happen. Either a switch from permadeath to a large EXP Points penalty. Similar to when you leave a run without doing anything. Or able to have multiple characters so I can choose when to risk a high level character or when I want to test the waters with a low level one.

And lastly as far as technical aspects go. 
-Combat. While I like the feel of it already I think it could do with just a bit more weight behind the player strikes. Not necessarily more damage but just from the animation itself possibly to relay a bit more impact.
-Torches. I have already seen a lot of folks talk about this one but wanted to throw it in just in case. I actually stopped using them as it made it so hard to see. Definitely could use some adjustments.
-Climbing/Ledge Grabbing. While Ledge grabbing might make it too easy for people to cheese some areas of the maps I would love the ability to at least climb up onto another reachable walkable surface or climb over a fence. Just to add a bit more versatility in the exploration/desperate escape attempts. lol 

All that being said this game has an awesome vibe and a lot of potential. Looking forward to playing this more.

Expedition: Into Darkness, is setting up to be medieval Tarkov. So far the demo is "many good ideas," as well as adaptations to the existing ones from other games. Its a janky mess but it's also a demo, they were smarter than most to not immediately slap the "Early Access" label on there. Bravo Antediluvian Interactive, I see a bright future here!

The Good Stuff:
- DEEP Weapon Customization! 👷 Shaping up to be on par with Tarkov, but in a medieval setting. Sickk.
- Exploration! 🗺️ Seamless transitions, treasure absolutely everywhere, I just wish I could jump bro...
- World Bosses/Elites! 💀 Yes. More of this, yes. Yes. (add NPC mercenaries too please!)
- Build! 🏡 Just like in Arc Raiders & Tarkov, build up your home, make life easier.
- PvE! 😈 I prefer PvE. Good to see PvE enjoyers eating good. 
- 5 Players! 🫂 I hope we can get a raid system in the future, a man can dream.

The Needs Work:
- Combat! ⚔️ Its just flat out boring after an hour or so. It feels light. It feels floaty. It needs work.
- Optimization! 🖥️ Not gonna beat a dead horse. They know it, we know it, move on.
- Menus! 📜 They are lacking, no sound effects on clicks, moving items is sluggish at best. ALT + Click doesn't move to the open bag. Help. Just please send help.
- Darkness! 🌚 Torches and Lanterns I know... A Gamma slider option would be appreciated, its PvE.

+Recommended, will get better. As long as the devs keep up the good work, we're looking at an amazing gaming experience for hardcore players, an easy ride for people who want to just chill with friend, and a loot goblins absolute paradise.
Optimization, combat system rework/revamp, and menu touch ups are my complaints, and I still played the game for 2 hours straight. I look forward to see the next steps for this game. 🙇🏻‍♂️

I love this game. I've played this demo and the two playtest available before this demo. The feeling of the game on the first playtest I played was my favorite, with this demo being my second favorite. I love how far it has come and I am excited to see how far this will go. 

Combat is clunky but meaningful. might not be for everyone. I miss putting bags within bags within bags within bags within even more bags, but I under stand putting a limit on such. 

Inventory management is easy when you are familiar with this style of inventory system, but I believe certain actions should be clarified and given context clues/ keybind hints. I know you can rotate with R when holding something, but I have not seen any keybind hint. 

There are certain bosses that I have no idea how I would approach while playing solo. for example the huge orge in Moor. But I had 1 friend with me. we couldn't find the blacksmith key so i figured we should let the ogre break down the door. successful, but then we still had to deal with the ogre. my buddy and i would take turns attacking its butt while it was aggroed on the other, but when the ogre picked up my friend i rushed in and killed it before we could see what happened. super tense and will be a core memory when i think about this game. shoutout to my friend for reviving me twice during that fight. revive time and general interaction time takes a little too long. 

The lack of jump is meh, but lack of crouch feels really annoying. the walk keybind doesnt seem to actually do anything at the current time I played. switching the walking mechanic for crouching would feel more impactful on the player and visually apparent that you "are stealthing"
